# Animate from video

Convert recorded human performance from supplied video to editable Blender body
animation that a 3D character copies; AI clips stay with make-ai-video.

Convert source-performance timing to editable raw and cleaned actions; compare
both against the video. [blender](../SKILL.md) owns scene
authorship, render budgets and delivery; this reference owns extraction, retargeting
and motion cleanup.

## Choose a route the shot can support

Use the registration-free local route on qualified macOS Apple Silicon:
[setup and extraction](local.md) → [Rigify scene motion](scene-motion.md).
On first execution, invoke
`scripts/run.py extract`; it lazily downloads missing runtime/model assets into a
persistent cache. Later runs support `--offline`. Blender remains an installed prerequisite.

The tested scene route combines captured body directions with **authored** room
travel, height, foot paths, seat support and prop-relative hand contacts. Keep that
distinction visible in the preview. MediaPipe does not recover room geometry or
measured jump height. The walk/sit/reach example explicitly reconstructs hidden legs;
it is not fully automatic walking. The adapter supports its generated Rigify basic-human
fixture, not arbitrary character rigs. Fingers, reliable twist and full collision
handling remain outside the qualified route.

For an in-place comparison, [local.md](local.md) also documents the smaller
reference adapter. For another backend, check exact weights, code and body-model
terms separately. SMPL-X registration and GVHMR are not needed for the default route.

## Retarget and clean deliberately

Inspect the supplied scene with [inspect-rig.py](../scripts/inspect-rig.py). The reference
adapter creates its own fixed rig and
rejects an existing scene. Write a dedicated adapter or custom Blender script for
another character, on a copy with saved checkpoints.

The reference helper accepts manually reviewed intervals; it does not detect contacts.

# CG into footage or a photo

For CG in the user's video or photo of a real place: the plate keeps its pixels, and the work is where CG meets
it. Shadow catching needs Cycles. Verified in Blender 5.2.0 against synthetic plates with a known camera.

## Track, solve and orient (video)

```python
clip = bpy.data.movieclips.load(path)                   # absolute path: an .mp4, or a sequence's first frame
last = scene.frame_end = clip.frame_duration; scene.frame_start = 1
clip.tracking.camera.focal_length_pixels = lens_35mm * max(clip.size) / 36   # 35 mm equiv.; in px, 9:16 works
s, k = clip.tracking.settings, clip.size[0] / 640       # tracker sizes tuned at 640 px wide
s.default_pattern_size, s.default_search_size, s.default_margin = int(21 * k) | 1, int(120 * k), int(10 * k)
s.default_motion_model, s.use_keyframe_selection = "Perspective", True   # fixed keyframes 1, 30 fail short clips
s.refine_intrinsics_focal_length = True                 # unless the focal length is known exactly
win = bpy.context.window_manager.windows[0]; area = win.screen.areas[0]; area.type = "CLIP_EDITOR"
space = area.spaces.active; space.clip = clip; rec = clip.tracking.reconstruction
ctx = dict(window=win, area=area, region=next(r for r in area.regions if r.type == "WINDOW"),
           space_data=space, edit_movieclip=clip)
with bpy.context.temp_override(**ctx):                  # clip operators run headless only inside this
    for frame, back in ((1, False), (last // 2, False), (last // 2, True), (last, True)):
        scene.frame_set(frame); space.clip_user.frame_current = frame   # the editor ignores frame_set
        bpy.ops.clip.detect_features(margin=16, threshold=0.1, min_distance=int(0.06 * clip.size[0]))
        bpy.ops.clip.track_markers(backwards=back, sequence=True)
    bpy.ops.clip.clean_tracks(frames=10, error=0, action="DELETE_TRACK")
    for _ in range(4):
        try: bpy.ops.clip.solve_camera()
        except RuntimeError: break                      # too few tracks left
        if rec.average_error <= 0.3: break
        bpy.ops.clip.clean_tracks(frames=10, error=max(0.3, 2 * rec.average_error), action="DELETE_TRACK")
```

- Bowed straight lines (action cams, ultra-wides): add `s.refine_intrinsics_radial_distortion = True` (on a clean
  plate it skewed the focal length 6%). A pure pan: `s.use_tripod_solver = True`, then place the floor by eye.

Floor: fit a plane (numpy SVD) to bundles in the lower 45% of the middle frame, keep those within 2% of their
spread (refit 3 times), and take the widest triangle of 3 as `a, b, c` (0.2–0.5° of tilt; random 3: 0.6–6.9°).

```python
cam, sel = scene.camera, lambda *picked: [setattr(t, "select", t in picked) for t in clip.tracking.tracks]
with bpy.context.temp_override(**ctx):
    sel(a, b, c); bpy.ops.clip.set_plane(plane="FLOOR")
    sel(a); bpy.ops.clip.set_origin()                   # a: where the CG stands
    M = cam.matrix_basis; h = (M @ rec.cameras.matrix_from_frame(frame=last // 2)).translation.z
    sel(a, b); bpy.ops.clip.set_scale(distance=(M @ a.bundle - M @ b.bundle).length * held_m / h)
    bpy.ops.clip.set_active_clip()                      # render size = clip size
cam.constraints.new("CAMERA_SOLVER")                    # follows scene.active_clip
cam.data.sensor_fit, cam.data.sensor_width = "AUTO", 36
cam.data.lens = clip.tracking.camera.focal_length_pixels * 36 / max(clip.size)
```

`held_m`: camera height above the floor (handheld phone 1.3–1.6 m), or pass a known `a`–`b` distance. This
replaces `setup_tracking_scene()`, whose holdout layer kept every shadow off the plate. `scene.render.fps` = the
source's (`clip.fps` reads 0 for a sequence). A photo: EXIF `FocalLengthIn35mmFilm` on `sensor_width` 36.

## Composite, light and colour

- `ground.is_shadow_catcher = True` under every shadow, `view_layer.cycles.use_pass_shadow_catcher = True`,
  `film_transparent = True`; plate (`CompositorNodeMovieClip` or `CompositorNodeImage`) × `Shadow Catcher` pass
  (ShaderNodeMix RGBA MULTIPLY, Factor 1, inputs 6, 7, output 2) → `CompositorNodeAlphaOver` Background, Render
  Layers `Image` → Foreground. Real objects in front of the CG: proxy meshes, also shadow catchers.
- Plate in reflections and bounce: catcher and proxies get a Mix Shader, Fac = Light Path `Is Camera Ray`, socket 1
  an Emission of the plate (Image Texture, Texture Coordinate `Window`, extension EXTEND, for a sequence
  `image_user.use_auto_refresh` and `frame_duration`), socket 2 a Diffuse of it.
- Sun: `to_sun` = normalize(bundle at a vertical edge's top − bundle at its shadow tip),
  `sun.rotation_euler = to_sun.to_track_quat("Z", "Y").to_euler()`, angle 0.526°. Strength: the Shadow Catcher
  pass in the CG umbra within 10% of shadow ÷ lit on one ground material in linear plate pixels. A CG-only light
  that should light the real ground: `is_shadow_catcher = False`.
- sRGB or Rec.709 plates (phone video, JPEG): `view_transform = "Standard"`, look None (AgX over everything moved
  98% of plate pixels). AgX on the CG only: `CompositorNodePremulKey` (To Straight) → `CompositorNodeConvertToDisplay`
  (`view_settings` AgX) → `CompositorNodeConvertColorSpace` (sRGB → Linear Rec.709) → Alpha Over, Straight Alpha on.
  Log plates: the clip's colour space (`"Apple Log"`, `"ARRI LogC4"`, `"S-Log3 S-Gamut3.Cine"`), one view transform.
- CG only, on straight colour: Blur 0.5–1 px; light wrap on bright plates (plate blurred 2% of width ×
  Blur(1 − α, 1% of width) × α, added at 0.1–0.3); blacks lifted to the plate's 0.5th percentile (Color Balance
  ASC-CDL, Offset colour `inputs[10]`); grain matched to the plate's ([render and grade](render-and-grade.md)).
- Lens distortion: `CompositorNodeMovieDistortion` (Distort, `clip` set) on the CG; shadow as plate − plate ×
  Distort(Invert(Shadow Catcher)), since distorting the pass itself blackens the frame edges.
- Motion blur: match the plate's streaks (daylight phone video is about 1/500 s, shutter 0.06 at 30 fps).

# Camera moves and lenses

Shot grammar is in [cinematography](../../make-ai-video/references/continuity.md). Here a
shot becomes a camera: `scripts/camera-rig.py` keys the move, aims at the subject every frame with a level
horizon, and binds each shot's camera with a timeline marker at its first frame.

| Shot | Move and params | Lens | Timing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Push in | `dolly`, `push` 1–2 | 35–50 mm | 4–6 s |
| Pull back | `dolly`, `push` −2 to −4 | 24–35 mm | 4–6 s |
| Reveal, rise + pull back | `jib`, `distance` → `distance_to`, `height` → `height_to` | 24–35 mm | 5–8 s |
| Detail, then reveal | any move, `aim` the detail (an object or point) → `aim_to` `subject` | 35–50 mm | 4–6 s |
| Low-angle hero | `static` or `dolly`, `height` 0.3–0.6 | 18–25 mm | 3–5 s |
| Orbit | `orbit`, `heading` → `heading_to` 90–180° apart, `distance` 3–6 | 35–50 mm | 6–10 s |
| Tracking | `dolly`, `push` 0, `follow` true; or `from`/`to` points, aimed at the subject or an `aim` point | 35–50 mm | the action |
| Handheld | `handheld`, `shake` 0.5–2 | 24–35 mm | any |
| Dutch | any move, `roll` 10–25 | any | — |
| Vertigo | `dolly-zoom`, `distance` → `distance_to` (×2 or ×½) | 35–50 mm | 3–5 s |
| Crash zoom | lens `zoom` `{"to": 100, "at": 12, "frames": 6}` | zoom | 4–8 frames |

A shot takes `name`, `move`, `start`, `end` (frames), `subject` (an object or `[x, y, z]`), `params` and
`lens`. `heading` 0 puts the camera on the subject's −Y side; `height` is above the ground under the
subject. `aim` (`subject`, `locked`, an object name or `[x, y, z]`) moves to `aim_to` over the shot. Lens: `focal` (mm), `sensor` (`super35`, `full-frame`, `super16`), `fstop` (`null` for no depth
of field), `focus` (`subject` or metres), `shutter` (degrees; 180 = `motion_blur_shutter` 0.5).
`python3 "$skill/scripts/camera-rig.py" --list` prints every parameter and default.

```json
{"shots": [
  {"name": "Reveal", "move": "jib", "start": 1, "end": 120, "subject": "Car",
   "params": {"heading": 20, "distance": 2.5, "height": 0.4, "distance_to": 8, "height_to": 3.5},
   "lens": {"focal": 24, "fstop": 4}},
  {"name": "Turn", "move": "orbit", "start": 121, "end": 240, "subject": "Car",
   "params": {"heading": 30, "heading_to": 150, "distance": 6, "height": 1.2},
   "lens": {"focal": 50, "fstop": 2}}
]}
```

```sh
blender -b "$work/scene.blend" --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 \
  --python "$skill/scripts/camera-rig.py" -- "$work/shots.json" "$work/shot.blend"
```

Preview at half size and 16 samples, look at the draft, then render the hero frames from the same file
at full settings and finish them with `--intent deliver`.

```sh
blender -b "$work/shot.blend" --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 \
  --python-expr "import bpy; s = bpy.context.scene; s.render.resolution_percentage = 50; s.cycles.samples = 16; s.cycles.use_denoising = True" \
  -o "$work/review/preview/####" -F PNG -a
voyager blender finalize "$work/review/preview" --fps 24 --draft
```

# Asset sources

For licences, receipts and credits of third-party assets, and where free game art, icons, palettes, plugins and animations come from.

## Core

- Each grabbed asset gets a receipt `<asset-id>.json` beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`, `attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a line in the project's `CREDITS`: title, author, source URL, licence.
- `voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` searches Poly Haven (CC0 textures, HDRIs, models), ambientCG (CC0 materials, HDRIs), Kenney (CC0 packs), game-icons.net and Incompetech; `voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` saves under `assets/<source>/<id>/` with the receipt and the `CREDITS` line. Poly Haven asks that users are told its assets come from Poly Haven.
- Kenney (kenney.nl): CC0 whole packs (2D, 3D, UI, audio, textures); search matches pack names and categories only. Packs include `License.txt`.
- game-icons.net: CC BY 3.0 (a few authors CC0), credited per icon's author. Each SVG is a black square path under a white icon path; recolour or drop them via `fill`.
- Incompetech: Kevin MacLeod's music, CC BY 4.0 with his credit text; fetch single tracks only.
- Lospec: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json` returns name, author (sometimes empty; the palette page names the creator) and hex colours. Credit "<palette> by <author> (Lospec)".
- Godot Asset Library: keyless JSON at `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (without `godot_version` it returns nothing); `cost` holds the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`. Plugins and scripts, not art. The new Godot Asset Store (beta, no public API) is replacing it.
- OpenGameArt: no API. Search pages (`/art-search-advanced?keys=…`) only; robots.txt sets a 10 s crawl delay and disallows `/search/`. Licences (often several, including SA and GPL) and the attribution text are on each content page.
- Mixamo: Adobe's terms forbid access other than through its interface and any data mining, so the user downloads in their own browser; Voyager imports and rigs the FBX. Raw characters and animations are not redistributable.
- itch.io: no search API (every endpoint needs auth and covers your own account); tag pages have RSS (`itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-<tag>.xml`) without licences. Licences are free text per page; the user downloads, and pays where needed.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. When the audio is a person's recording, review the processed voice stem (not the final mix with music) and pass the recording as `--audio-source`: review then flags a noise floor raised more than 15 dB or crushed dynamics; never force a very quiet recording to the target.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Field notes

## FPV and camera moves

- Wide 18–22 mm lenses and interpolated banked roll sell FPV; measure each camera's closest distance to visible geometry to catch clipping before rendering.
- Motion previews need every frame at the actual fps; skipped frames conceal speed and clearance problems.

## Product and CAD films

- Native CAD assemblies preserve placements and colors better than mesh exports; convert with a CAD kernel and verify part count and bounds against the source.
- Rig from the assembly's joint anchors and axes, cross-checking kinematics files.
- Focus macros on the visible face, using ray-cast focus rather than part origins; keep separation and the exploded hold in one continuous camera to avoid apparent jumps.
- Unit mismatches break depth of field and texture grain; motion blur can pulse unevenly and may need disabling per shot.

## Compositing into live action

- A distant insert without meaningful parallax can use a smoothed 2D similarity track on consistent distant landmarks; measure residual jitter before attempting a full camera solve.
- Render transparent inserts at their on-screen size; keep them opaque and add haze color rather than lowering opacity to fake distance.
- Solidify can produce shading artifacts under hard light; bake the modifier and fix normals when it does.

## Car films

- Drive wheels from distance traveled on one continuous road so cuts read as coverage of one drive.
- Check cut pairs in motion: similar angles at different distances make a car jump or shrink, while cameras locked to its center create accidental match cuts.
- Near-360° camera rotation between frames can flash at cuts; retiming shallow-focus shots also requires re-pinning focus.

## Previs to photoreal

- Tell the editing model that video controls cameras, cuts and timing while images control appearance; state exact character counts and check reference prop placement to avoid duplicates.
- Rough mannequin limbs can transfer as stiff acting; avoid asking for natural performance and preservation of every pose in the same prompt.
- Send clean previs without labels or watermarks; generated cuts can shift by a frame and output dimensions can drift, so realign at assembly.
- Repair a defective shot as a targeted segment edit and splice back only its frames.

## Cost and render-time calibration

Historical measurements below calibrate rough estimates, not current prices or hardware guarantees; benchmark the actual scene and route.

- A 30 s, 24 fps Eevee preview at 960×540 took about 16 min locally; a selected seven-shot 1080p Eevee cut took about 20 min on four Voyager GPUs and about 320 credits, with CPU/RAM omitted from the lower pre-quote.
- A 517-part CAD film, 34 s at 1680×720, took about 35–40 min on a laptop GPU in Cycles at 32 samples.
- A dense 11 s car film had 5–7 min local low-resolution previews and a final costing about 2,700 Voyager GPU credits; do not extrapolate the cheaper FPV render to detailed car scenes.
- Distant Cycles CPU inserts rendered at on-screen size took about 2–4 s/frame; full-frame sprite renders waste that advantage.
- A 1080p Seedance 2.5 editing take took 10–13 min, with an estimated cost of $1.50–2 per output second; re-estimate with the live route before spending.
- Check engine support on each cloud route before quoting; switching engines changes an approved look, and mixing renderers or denoisers within a shot causes discontinuity.
- Paid per-frame time limits can bill failed frames; test one frame without blindly retrying failed probes.
- Heavy scenes can crash local GPUs; render per shot and resume only failed frames rather than risking a whole-film restart.

# Rigged characters: clothes and body types

Use this when the deliverable is a **rigged, skinned 3D character that must move** (a game, an
engine import, an animated 3D scene) and it wears clothes, or one outfit must fit several bodies.

Not for: changing clothes in an image or video, concept art, character sheets, turnarounds or stills
of a character. Those stay with make-image, make-ai-video and the project's Elements; never move them into
Blender or a 3D model.

## Pick a route

| The user wants | Route |
|---|---|
| Characters that look like a concept, outfit never swapped | A. Generate each dressed character as one mesh, then auto-rig |
| One outfit on many body types, matching exactly; or swappable clothes on a human base | B. MakeHuman base (MPFB) with its fitted clothes |
| Their own garment on their own rigged body | C. Fit it in Blender, hide the body under it, check |

## A. One dressed mesh, then auto-rig

1. Draw the character with make-image in a neutral A-pose, front view, whole body, plain background.
   For other body types, edit that image with it as the reference ("the same outfit, worn by a tall
   thin man"), so the outfit stays the same. Image models soften big proportion changes: say so in the
   prompt and check the result.
2. Generate each mesh: `meshy:image-to-3d` with `pose_mode: "a-pose"`, `should_texture: true`,
   `should_remesh: true` and a `target_polycount` for the game (about 30,000 for a hero). `meshy:` models
   need a paid Voyager plan; otherwise fal's `meshy/v7.1/image-to-3d` with `enable_rigging: true` does
   generation and rigging in one call.
3. Rig: `meshy:rigging` with `input_task_id` (the generation's `task_id`) and `height_meters`. It is
   humanoid only and wants a textured mesh under 300,000 faces. The rigged GLB has 24 Mixamo-style bones
   (`Hips`, `Spine`, `LeftArm`, `LeftForeArm`, `LeftUpLeg`, `LeftLeg`, ...) and a walk and a run clip;
   `meshy:animations` adds preset actions to the same rig. Tripo's rig API (`spec: "mixamo"`) is the
   alternative.
4. Import with `fetch-model.py` or `bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf`; Meshy's GLB has the armature at 0.01
   scale and a stray `Icosphere` to delete.

## B. MakeHuman base (MPFB)

MPFB (GPL-3.0 add-on; its bodies, clothes and rigs are CC0, and exported characters carry no licence
claim) builds human bodies from sliders and fits each MakeHuman garment to the body shape. Every garment
hides the body under it, so collars, armpits and shoes stay closed on every body type.

```sh
export BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES="$work/blender-user"
blender --online-mode --command extension install -s -e mpfb
# Clothes, skins and hair: the CC0 system assets (about 280 MB) go into MPFB's user data folder.
curl -L -o "$work/assets.zip" https://files2.makehumancommunity.org/asset_packs/makehuman_system_assets/makehuman_system_assets_cc0.zip
unzip -q "$work/assets.zip" -d "$BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES/extensions/.user/blender_org/mpfb/data"
```

Then build every body type in one scene:

```sh
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python <this skill>/scripts/mpfb-outfit.py -- --out characters.blend \
  --body slim:gender=1,weight=0.1,muscle=0.3,height=0.7 --body average:gender=1 \
  --body heavy:gender=1,weight=1,muscle=0.7,height=0.3 --clothes male_casualsuit03,shoes01 --export glb
```

Macros run 0..1 (`gender`, `age`, `muscle`, `weight`, `proportions`, `height`, `cupsize`,
`firmness`). `--rig game_engine` (default) has Unreal-style bones; `mixamo` matches Mixamo
animations. The library's clothes are listed when a name is wrong. A new garment works only when it was
modelled over the MakeHuman body; MPFB's MakeClothes tools turn it into a `.mhclo`.

## C. Fit a garment to a body

For a garment made for one body that must go on another. Works best when the bodies share a mesh (body
types as shape keys of one body). Verified on Blender 5.2: fitted, then checked in four poses.

1. Bind the garment to the body it was made for: `SURFACE_DEFORM` with `target` the body, then
   `bpy.ops.object.surfacedeform_bind(modifier=...)` under `temp_override(object=garment)`; check
   `is_bound`. Use a copy of the body without helper or loose geometry, or binding fails.
2. Morph that body to the new shape (shape key value 1). The garment follows.
3. Add `SHRINKWRAP` with `wrap_method "NEAREST_SURFACEPOINT"`, `wrap_mode "OUTSIDE"`, `offset` 3–5 mm
   (pushes cloth that sank into the body back out, leaves the rest), then `CORRECTIVE_SMOOTH`.
4. Bake it: `garment.data = bpy.data.meshes.new_from_object(garment.evaluated_get(dg), depsgraph=dg)`, then
   clear its modifiers. `bpy.ops.object.convert` acts on the selection, not the override.
5. Weights: when the garment already has weights for a skeleton with the same bone names, keep them.
   Only a garment without weights gets them from the body (`DATA_TRANSFER`, `VGROUP_WEIGHTS`,
   `POLYINTERP_NEAREST`, names to names), after the garment sits on the new body; then
   `vertex_group_limit_total(limit=4)` and `vertex_group_normalize_all`. Body-transferred weights pulled
   the collar into the head and opened gaps at the hips when posed; kept weights did not.
6. Parent to the new rig with an `ARMATURE` modifier first in the stack.
7. Hide the body under the garment: body vertices whose normal ray hits the garment within 3 cm, minus one
   ring at each opening (collar, cuffs, hem), plus the whole foot under shoes; put them in a group and
   add a `MASK` with `invert_vertex_group = True`.

## Fit check

```sh
blender -b --factory-startup characters.blend --python-exit-code 1 --python <this skill>/scripts/outfit-check.py -- --out review/fit
```

It poses every rig (rest, arms up, stride, arms down), counts skin poking through cloth and hidden body
left uncovered, names the body region of each, and writes a front and side still per pose with the
problems marked (front: everyone in a row; side: one still per character). Fix what it names, rerun, then show the stills. A few vertices at a cuff or collar edge
are tolerable; tens in one region are a visible fault. Fingers or arms entering the hips of a wide body
in a pose are a pose problem (widen that animation for this body), not a fit problem. It checks
separate garments only; for route A it is a pose test of the stills.

Before export, apply the masks or delete the hidden faces in the export copy, and say which engine bone
names the rig uses.

# Glossy products

For a painted, lacquered or polished hero object whose reflections show its shape: a car, phone, bottle,
headphones, an appliance. These are starting points for a photoreal brief; the user's brief, a reference
image or a saved look note wins, and matte, organic or stylized subjects can skip this guide. Values verified
in Blender 5.2.0 Cycles.

## Paint and coat

- Specular IOR Level 0, so the coat carries the reflection: at the default 0.5 the base adds a grey haze around every reflection (black paint between two strip lights read 0.89 linear, against 0.02).

## Glass, metal, plastic

- Glass modelled as one face (windows, screen covers): Transmission Weight 1, Roughness 0, IOR 1.52, Base Color (0.984, 0.995, 0.995), `Thin Wall` on (5.2+); without it the face refracts like the front of a solid block and shifts what is behind it. Eevee renders it once `scene.eevee.use_raytracing` and the material's `use_raytrace_refraction` are both True.
- An imported glTF keeps Coat, Transmission, IOR and Specular Tint but loses Thin Wall and Thin Film: set Thin Wall on single-sheet glass, Specular IOR Level 0 and Coat Weight 1 on paint, and turn Alpha-faded glass into Transmission 1, Alpha 1.

# Local reference path

Qualified on Apple M2 Pro, macOS arm64, Blender 5.2.2. Other platforms and Blender
versions are unqualified.

## Isolated setup

Set `skill` to this skill directory and `work` to a task-owned folder in the project (the piece's folder). **The first extraction** invokes
this launcher to download missing assets; it never installs into Blender or system
Python. On macOS 14+ Apple Silicon:

```sh
python3 "$skill/scripts/run.py" status
python3 "$skill/scripts/run.py" extract "$work/source.mp4" "$work/raw.jsonl"
# Subsequent extraction, with downloads forbidden:
python3 "$skill/scripts/run.py" --offline extract "$work/other.mp4" "$work/other.jsonl"
```

The launcher needs a working Python 3.9+ for bootstrap (Blender's bundled Python may
be used). Blender and FFmpeg for previews are separate installed
application prerequisites; the launcher does not install them.

Setup runs Voyager's `uv` (`voyager uv`, on a Voyager session's PATH), so the interpreter and
wheel downloads share the profile's `$VOYAGER_HOME/uv` cache. The environment and model go in
`$VOYAGER_HOME/cache/mocap`, or `~/Library/Application Support/Voyager/cache/mocap`.
`--cache-dir "$work/cache"` overrides that; **automated tests also set an isolated
`VOYAGER_HOME`**. The qualified setup used about 1.6 GB including Python, installed packages
and download caches.

`setup` warms the cache explicitly; `status` neither creates directories nor downloads. Remove the
affected revision folder to rebuild a damaged environment; keep models for reuse.

GVHMR's code license restricts commercial use, and its SMPL-family body assets
require separate registration; keep the default route registration-free.

## Extract and inspect

For room travel and contacts on a Rigify control rig, continue with
[scene-motion.md](scene-motion.md). The generated in-place reference below remains
a smaller baseline and does not preserve jump height.

`--max-frames 1800` is the default extraction budget.

The output is exclusive-create JSON Lines: a `voyager.pose/1` header, frame records,
and a completion summary. An interrupted/budget-exceeded file lacks the summary
and must not be imported.
Landmark order is MediaPipe's 33-point order; each point is
`[x, y, z, visibility, presence]`. Missing poses are null.

No frame-rate conversion is performed. Normalize rotated footage with FFmpeg first, preserving timing and
recording the original hash and transform.

```sh
BLENDER_USER_CONFIG="$work/blender-config" blender -b -t 2 --factory-startup \
  --python-exit-code 1 --python "$skill/scripts/reference-rig.py" -- \
  "$work/raw.jsonl" "$work/animation.blend" --contacts "$work/contacts.json" \
  --render 1,40,120
```

Omit `--contacts` when no intervals have been reviewed. Its JSON is a list:
`[{"side":"L","start":2.65,"end":3.10}]`, in elapsed source seconds. These example
times belong to the validation clip only. The adapter needs at least 3 observations
and refuses to overwrite a checkpoint or load another rig.

The output contains `Mocap_Raw` and `Mocap_Cleaned`, each retained with a fake user
on its own armature, and an adjacent `.report.json`.
Raw means retargeted from original observations; both actions use the same roll
stabilization and authored floor placement. Cleaned additionally interpolates short
low-confidence gaps, lightly smooths selected limb endpoints and applies contact IK.

**Root placement is authored:** horizontal pelvis position stays fixed and height
is fitted to the lowest foot mesh vertex. This destroys jump height; a walking source
will move its limbs in place. Floor fitting does
not solve hand contact, body collision or chair interaction.

Two-bone IK clamps unreachable targets and the report counts them; the cleaned action
gets editable pelvis-height correction keys where feet penetrate the floor. Blender
uses 30 fps with fractional key times (`1 + elapsed * 30`), so VFR samples retain their times.

After a `start:end` `--render`, the scripts print the `voyager blender finalize`
command to run on its frames folder; a frame list such as `1,40,120` stays as
review stills.

# Match a reference image

```sh
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python <this skill>/scripts/compare-reference.py -- \
  --reference ref.png --render review/still.png --out review/compare.png --grid \
  --object donut=0.14,0.3,0.42,0.58/0.13,0.29,0.43,0.59 --object glaze=0.19,0.39,0.31,0.22/0.18,0.36,0.33,0.22 \
  --object mug-body=0.62,0.17,0.18,0.25/0.63,0.24,0.17,0.18 --object table=0.7,0.6,0.28,0.38
```

Output opens with one `COMPARE_OBJECT <name>:` line per object: `look matches the reference`, or each
look gap with the change that closes it, for example `highlights: smaller (area 4% vs 14%), crisper ...
→ raise roughness`. Gaps cover colour (hue, saturation, value, warmth), highlights (size, strength,
sharpness: glossy or matte), texture (fine detail, broad mottling, grain scale, visible tiling),
contrast (tonal range, shadow depth) and edges (outline softness, glow, light passing through). A box
with plain background around its object is measured on the object's own pixels; the sheet dims what
was left out, so check it. Otherwise the whole box is measured, so keep surface boxes inside the
surface. When the object is not found on its own (a dark mug on a dark wall; the line ends
`[measured on the whole box ...]`), pass `--mask <name>=<image>` for the reference and
`--render-mask <name>=<image>` for the render: a full-frame image, white or opaque on the object (a still
with Film > Transparent on and every other object's `visible_camera` off). A hard light/shadow edge
across a box is reported as light, not material. A `COMPARE_REFERENCE_FRAME (advisory)` line follows with
framing, whole-frame and regional tone numbers (which third of the frame is too bright or dark).

# Organic liquids: drips, glaze, sauce, melt, pour

For any liquid or soft matter that flows over a surface under gravity: icing and glaze, chocolate or
caramel sauce, honey, syrup, melting wax or ice cream, paint. A stylized brief that asks for uniform or
cartoon drips wins. The snippets below run as-is in Blender 5.2; they are building blocks, and the look
is judged against real photos (see [match a reference](match-a-reference.md)).

## Glaze and icing with drips

`glaze_coat` builds the coat over a round host (a donut, cake, bun, cupcake) as one shell: it follows
the host's top, ends in a wavy rounded lip at `edge`, and hangs `drip_layout`'s tongues from that lip,
flat on the side, flaring into it at the root and ending in elongated tips. It never touches the host.

```python
import math
import random

import bmesh
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector


def drip_layout(count, longest, width, edge, rng):
    """Each drip's place along the coat's edge (0-1 around it), length below the lip, half-width and tip
    half-width: close pairs and threes, gaps, about a fifth bumps that barely leave the lip, mostly short
    tongues and two long runs. width: a tongue's half-width. edge: the lip's length in metres; neighbours
    keep about three widths apart so they never fuse into one blob, so a short edge holds fewer than count.
    """
    gap, spots = 3 * width * 1.25 / edge, []
    count = min(count, int(0.6 / gap))  # room for the spacing, with gaps left between runs
    for _ in range(count * 50):
        if len(spots) == count:
            break
        at = rng.random()  # runs of one to three close neighbours from random points, gaps between
        for _ in range(rng.choice((1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3))):
            if len(spots) < count and all(min(abs(at - o), 1 - abs(at - o)) >= gap for o in spots):
                spots.append(at)
            at = (at + gap * rng.uniform(1.0, 1.6)) % 1.0
    kinds = ["long"] * 2 + ["bump"] * round(len(spots) / 5)
    kinds = (kinds + ["short"] * len(spots))[: len(spots)]
    rng.shuffle(kinds)
    drips = []
    for kind, at in zip(kinds, sorted(spots)):
        size = width * rng.uniform(0.65, 1.4)
        bead = size * rng.uniform(1.1, 1.25)
        length = (longest * rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0) if kind == "long"
                  else rng.uniform(0.0, bead) if kind == "bump"
                  else longest * rng.uniform(0.12, 0.6))
        drips.append({"at": at, "length": length, "width": size, "bead": bead})
    return drips


def glaze_coat(name, host, edge, drips, thickness, material):
    """A glaze or icing poured over a round host: one shell hugging its top, ending in a wavy, rounded lip
    at height `edge` (world z, metres), with drips that hang from that lip as flat tongues.

    drips: from drip_layout. Each tongue leaves the lip wide, like a curtain, runs down the side, and ends in
    an elongated, rounded tip; it lies flat on the host, thicker at the tip, with no neck. thickness: the
    coat's depth (1.5-2 mm on a donut). The host stays untouched; the coat is a new object.
    """
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_object(host, bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get())
    bm.transform(host.matrix_world)
    deepest = max((d["length"] for d in drips), default=0.0) + 2 * max((d["bead"] for d in drips), default=0.0)
    low, high = edge - deepest - 0.002, edge + 4 * thickness
    bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[f for f in bm.faces if max(v.co.z for v in f.verts) < low], context="FACES")
    # Fine faces where the lip and drips are shaped: about a quarter of the coat's depth.
    for _ in range(8):
        long = [e for e in bm.edges if e.calc_length() > thickness * 0.3
                and low < min(v.co.z for v in e.verts) and max(v.co.z for v in e.verts) < high]
        if not long:
            break
        bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(bm, edges=long, cuts=1, use_grid_fill=True)
    bm.normal_update()
    deform = bm.verts.layers.deform.verify()  # layers first: adding one later moves every vertex
    depth = bm.verts.layers.float.new("depth")
    middle = sum((Vector(c) for c in host.bound_box), Vector()) / 8
    middle = host.matrix_world @ middle
    rng = random.Random(len(drips))
    waves = [(rng.uniform(2, 5), rng.uniform(0, math.tau), thickness * rng.uniform(0.4, 0.9)) for _ in range(3)]
    for vert in bm.verts:
        offset = vert.co - middle
        angle, around = math.atan2(offset.y, offset.x), offset.to_2d().length
        below = edge + sum(a * math.sin(f * angle + p) for f, p, a in waves) - vert.co.z
        inside, tip, narrow = -below, 0.0, float("inf")  # distance into the coat, tip share, drip width
        # Drips hang only off the outer side, never into a hole: fade them out where the surface turns in.
        outward = min(max(4.0 * vert.normal.to_2d().dot(offset.to_2d().normalized()), 0.0), 1.0)
        for drip in drips if outward > 0.0 else ():
            across = abs(math.remainder(angle - drip["at"] * math.tau, math.tau)) * around
            reach, inner = _tongue(drip, across, below, thickness)
            reach -= (1.0 - outward) * 3.0 * drip["width"]
            # Smooth union: each tongue flares into the lip like a curtain instead of meeting it at a corner.
            inside = _smooth_max(inside, reach, 1.5 * drip["width"])
            tip = max(tip, inner * min(max(below / drip["bead"], 0.0), 1.0))  # tips swell below the lip only
            if reach > 0.0 and below > 0.0:
                narrow = min(narrow, drip["width"])
        lip = 1.0 + 0.4 * max(0.0, 1.0 - abs(below) / (4 * thickness)) + 0.4 * tip
        rise = min(max(inside, 0.0) / (1.2 * thickness), 1.0)  # a round lip: a quarter circle up from 0
        # A drip stays flat: never deeper than half its half-width, or it reads as a round tube with a ball.
        vert[depth] = min(thickness * lip, 0.5 * narrow) * math.sqrt(rise * (2.0 - rise))
    bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[f for f in bm.faces if all(v[depth] <= 0.0 for v in f.verts)], context="FACES")
    bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[v for v in bm.verts if not v.link_faces], context="VERTS")
    if not bm.verts:
        raise ValueError(f"glaze_coat: nothing to coat on {host.name}; is edge above its top?")
    most = max(v[depth] for v in bm.verts)
    for vert in bm.verts:
        vert.co -= vert.normal * thickness * 0.15  # start just under the host so the edge has no seam
        vert[deform][0] = vert[depth] / most
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
    bm.free()
    mesh.shade_smooth()
    mesh.materials.append(material)
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh)
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(obj)
    obj.vertex_groups.new(name="Depth")
    shell = obj.modifiers.new("Coat", "SOLIDIFY")
    shell.thickness, shell.offset, shell.vertex_group = most + thickness * 0.15, 1.0, "Depth"
    shell.thickness_vertex_group, shell.use_quality_normals = 0.0, True
    return obj


def _tongue(drip, across, below, thickness):
    """Signed distance into one drip's outline at (across, below) from its centre line and the lip, and how
    far into its tip (0-1). The tip is an ellipse 1.5x as long as wide."""
    width, bead, length = drip["width"], drip["bead"], drip["length"]
    stretch = 1.5
    centre = length - stretch * bead  # the tip ellipse's centre; its bottom is at `length`
    # Wide where it leaves the lip, tapering into the body, which swells and thins gently along its run.
    flare = 0.7 * math.exp(-max(below, 0.0) / (1.5 * width))
    swell = width * (1.0 + flare + 0.12 * math.sin(below / (2.5 * width) + drip["at"] * 40.0))
    body = swell - across if below <= centre else -1.0
    tip = bead - math.hypot(across, (below - centre) / stretch)
    return _smooth_max(body, tip, 0.6 * width), max(0.0, min(1.0, tip / bead))


def _smooth_max(a, b, k):
    h = max(k - abs(a - b), 0.0) / k
    return max(a, b) + h * h * k * 0.25
```

`glaze_coat("Glaze", donut, edge=z, drips=drip_layout(22, longest=0.012, width=0.0025, edge=2 * math.pi
* outer_radius, rng=random.Random(4)), thickness=0.0016, material=glaze)` with `edge` a little above the
host's widest point, so the tongues run over the bulge. `width` is a tongue's half-width at its body
(about the host's width / 35: 2.5 mm on a 9 cm donut, 6 mm on a 21 cm cake; read it off the reference)
and `thickness` the coat's depth (about a third of `width`), `longest` the longest run below the lip. Use the
values as they come; do not even out the spacing or lengths, but turn the whole layout (add the same
amount to every `at`) so the shot camera sees several drips, a long run among them, not a gap. Keep the coat's material smooth: no noise
bump beyond strength 0.02, or every highlight breaks into a wobbly streak.

## Pours and puddles

```python
import math

import bpy
from mathutils import Quaternion


def pour(name, top, floor_z, stream, pool, rng):
    """A thick liquid falling from top onto a flat surface at floor_z, pooled into one soft-edged puddle.

    One metaball family: the stream, the heap where it lands and the puddle blend into one surface with a
    rounded edge and no loose drops. In metres: stream is the radius where it leaves the top (honey about
    1.5-3 mm), pool the puddle's rough radius.
    """
    data = bpy.data.metaballs.new(name)
    # Metaball resolution cannot go below 5 mm in its own units, so the family is built in centimetres
    # and the object scaled by 0.01.
    data.resolution = data.render_resolution = stream * 100 * 0.25
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, data)
    obj.location, obj.scale = (top[0], top[1], floor_z), (0.01, 0.01, 0.01)
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(obj)
    height, stream, pool = (top[2] - floor_z) * 100, stream * 100, pool * 100
    # The stream thins as it falls. Balls spaced at 0.4x their radius blend into a smooth tube whose
    # surface sits at about 0.66x the ball radius; wider spacing shows as ribs.
    z = height
    while z > 0:
        element = data.elements.new(type="BALL")
        element.co = (0.0, 0.0, z)
        element.radius = stream * (1.0 - 0.35 * (1 - z / height)) / 0.66
        z -= element.radius * 0.4
    # A broad, low dome under the landing point, so the puddle's top curves (a flat top mirrors the room
    # in one hard band), and lobes of uneven reach for an irregular outline. Lobe centres sit below the
    # surface so the edge meets it at a shallow, rounded angle.
    dome = data.elements.new(type="ELLIPSOID")
    dome.co, dome.radius = (0.0, 0.0, -pool * 0.15), pool * 0.9
    dome.size_z = 0.55
    for _ in range(7):
        angle, reach = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi), pool * rng.uniform(0.25, 0.6)
        lobe = data.elements.new(type="ELLIPSOID")
        lobe.co = (math.cos(angle) * reach, math.sin(angle) * reach, -pool * 0.03)
        lobe.radius = pool * rng.uniform(0.45, 0.65)
        lobe.size_x, lobe.size_y, lobe.size_z = rng.uniform(1.0, 1.4), rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0), 0.25
        lobe.rotation = Quaternion((0.0, 0.0, 1.0), rng.uniform(0, math.pi))
    return obj
```

## Material

Honey, syrup and oil are clear, not opaque caramel: light passes through and picks up colour with
depth, so a thin stream is pale gold and a full jar deep amber. `clear_liquid` sets that up for Cycles:

```python
import math

import bpy


def clear_liquid(name, depth, tint=(0.85, 0.45, 0.07), roughness=0.06):
    """Honey, syrup, oil: a clear surface whose colour deepens with thickness (Cycles).

    depth: the thickness the camera mostly looks through, in metres (a jar's width, a puddle's depth).
    tint: the linear colour of white light after passing through that depth; thinner parts are paler,
    thicker parts darker. Default: golden honey. Needs a closed mesh with outward normals.
    """
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    nodes, link = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links.new
    bsdf = nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (1.0, 0.92, 0.75, 1.0)  # tint comes from the volume
    bsdf.inputs["Transmission Weight"].default_value = 1.0
    bsdf.inputs["IOR"].default_value = 1.49
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = roughness
    # Shadow rays pass through, tinted by the volume: Cycles lights what lies under or behind the liquid
    # only through caustics otherwise, so a puddle's wood and a jar's back wall turn muddy brown.
    mix = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMixShader")
    link(nodes.new("ShaderNodeLightPath").outputs["Is Shadow Ray"], mix.inputs["Fac"])
    link(bsdf.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1])
    link(nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent").outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
    link(mix.outputs[0], nodes["Material Output"].inputs["Surface"])
    volume = nodes.new("ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption")
    # Cycles absorbs density x (1 - Color) per metre; solve both so `depth` of it transmits `tint`.
    absorb = [-math.log(max(channel, 1e-4)) / depth for channel in tint]
    volume.inputs["Density"].default_value = max(absorb)
    volume.inputs["Color"].default_value = (*(1 - a / max(absorb) for a in absorb), 1.0)
    link(volume.outputs[0], nodes["Material Output"].inputs["Volume"])
    return mat
```

Set `scene.cycles.caustics_refractive = False` with it: with refractive caustics on, the light under the
liquid is counted twice and comes out brighter than bare ground. Give a jar's glass the same Is Shadow
Ray mix, or the ground under the jar renders black.

## Emissive states

A lit candle is a flame mesh plus a small warm point light at the flame (about 1800-2000 K), whose
warm pool on the wax, jar and table is what reads as lit. Build it with this (Cycles):

```python
import math

import bmesh
import bpy


def candle_flame(name, wick_top, height=0.022, kelvin=1850, watts=0.6):
    """A lit candle's flame on wick_top: a glowing teardrop and a warm point light in it (Cycles).

    The light, not the flame mesh, throws the warm pool onto the wax, jar and table, with soft shadows.
    0.6 W is a starting point beside a 3 W tabletop key about a metre away; a few watts floods the table orange.
    """
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere(bm, u_segments=24, v_segments=16, radius=1.0)
    for v in bm.verts:  # a teardrop: widest a quarter up, round at the base, drawn to a point at the tip
        t = (v.co.z + 1) / 2
        width = 0.18 * math.sin(math.pi * t**0.6) ** 0.8 / max(v.co.xy.length, 1e-6)
        v.co = (v.co.x * width, v.co.y * width, t)
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
    bm.free()
    mesh.shade_smooth()
    flame = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh)
    flame.location, flame.scale = wick_top, (height,) * 3
    # The point light lights the scene; the mesh only shows (lighting with both doubles the glow).
    flame.visible_shadow = flame.visible_diffuse = False
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(flame)
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}Glow")
    nodes, link = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links.new
    nodes.remove(nodes["Principled BSDF"])
    height_in_flame = nodes.new("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
    link(nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord").outputs["Generated"], height_in_flame.inputs[0])
    ramp = nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")  # dim blue base, yellow-white core, orange tip (linear colours)
    ramp.color_ramp.elements.new(0.15)
    ramp.color_ramp.elements.new(0.45)
    colors = ((0.05, 0.1, 0.6), (1.0, 0.42, 0.06), (1.0, 0.8, 0.45), (1.0, 0.3, 0.03))
    for element, color in zip(ramp.color_ramp.elements, colors):  # kept in order: 0, 0.15, 0.45, 1
        element.color = (*color, 1.0)
    link(height_in_flame.outputs["Z"], ramp.inputs["Fac"])
    glow = nodes.new("ShaderNodeEmission")
    glow.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 4.0  # brighter clips to flat white and loses the colours
    link(ramp.outputs["Color"], glow.inputs["Color"])
    edge = nodes.new("ShaderNodeLayerWeight")  # fade to clear at the silhouette: a soft edge, no outline
    edge.inputs["Blend"].default_value = 0.85
    mix = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMixShader")
    link(edge.outputs["Facing"], mix.inputs["Fac"])
    link(glow.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1])
    link(nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent").outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
    link(mix.outputs[0], nodes["Material Output"].inputs["Surface"])
    mat.cycles.emission_sampling = "NONE"
    mesh.materials.append(mat)
    light = bpy.data.lights.new(f"{name}Light", "POINT")
    light.use_temperature, light.temperature = True, kelvin
    light.energy, light.shadow_soft_size = watts, height * 0.3  # the flame's size: soft shadow edges
    lamp = bpy.data.objects.new(light.name, light)
    lamp.location = (wick_top[0], wick_top[1], wick_top[2] + height * 0.3)
    # A point light renders as a glowing ball, also through glass; let the flame mesh be what shows.
    lamp.visible_camera = lamp.visible_transmission = False
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(lamp)
    return flame, lamp


def candle_wax(name="Wax", color=(0.9, 0.8, 0.66)):
    """Candle wax that glows from within near the flame and passes a little warm light to the table.

    Deep subsurface carries the flame's light into the wax top, as in a photo of any lit candle. A share
    of shadow rays pass through, warm-tinted, so the wax body casts a soft warm shade, not a black disc.
    """
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    nodes, link = mat.node_tree.nodes, mat.node_tree.links.new
    bsdf = nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.35
    bsdf.inputs["Subsurface Weight"].default_value = 1.0
    bsdf.inputs["Subsurface Radius"].default_value = (1.0, 0.45, 0.2)
    bsdf.inputs["Subsurface Scale"].default_value = 0.015  # light travels about 1.5 cm into the wax
    through = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent")
    through.inputs["Color"].default_value = (1.0, 0.86, 0.7, 1.0)  # the flame is already orange: tint lightly
    share = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMath")
    share.operation, share.inputs[1].default_value = "MULTIPLY", 0.25  # 0: dark disc; 0.5: red smear at the base
    link(nodes.new("ShaderNodeLightPath").outputs["Is Shadow Ray"], share.inputs[0])
    mix = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMixShader")
    link(share.outputs[0], mix.inputs["Fac"])
    link(bsdf.outputs[0], mix.inputs[1])
    link(through.outputs[0], mix.inputs[2])
    link(mix.outputs[0], nodes["Material Output"].inputs["Surface"])
    return mat
```

# Render and grade

Cycles settings and finish for photoreal stills and frames, verified in Blender 5.2.0; GPU first: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

## Light paths

Keep the factory paths (caustics on, clamp direct 0 and indirect 10, Filter Glossy 1.0), except:
- steam, smoke, fog, clouds: `volume_bounces = 8`, 2 for thin haze (at the factory 0, dense white renders at 1/5);
  for heavy procedural or simulated smoke, fire and steam, `scene.cycles.volume_biased = True` ray-marches
  instead (much faster, slightly biased); a low `volume_max_steps` or a higher material `volume_step_rate`
  trades detail for speed. Keep the default unbiased path for subtle volumes where accuracy matters;
- stacked alpha cutouts (leaf, petal, hair cards): `transparent_max_bounces = 32`, 64 in dense canopies (past it, black);
- interiors lit by bounce: `diffuse_bounces = 8`, 12 with white walls (the factory 4 left a white room 0.5 EV
  dark, 12 within 0.1), and an Area light with `cycles.is_portal = True` in each window;
## Output

Stills and frames: PNG, which bakes in view, look and white balance; compare-reference measures it. A grading
master is OpenEXR, scene-linear with none of them: `image_settings.media_type = "MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE"` (5.x offers
the multilayer format only there), then `color_depth = "16"` and `exr_codec = "DWAA"`.

# Applying a scanned surface

A scanned material (Poly Haven, ambientCG) on a large surface such as a table, floor, wall or fabric
can still read as a flat sheet: the tile is stretched, the colour is flattened, the relief is weak and
the sheen is uniform. Download and wire a scan with this skill's [`scripts/fetch-material.py`](../scripts/fetch-material.py).
By default the material it builds already:

- sizes one tile from the scan's listed size (`--tile-size <metres>` overrides it) and, with the default
  box mapping, keeps that size when the object is scaled later;
- hides repeats with a second sample, turned and shifted, blended in through a noise mask. The default
  `--anti-tiling auto` skips bricks, tiles and planks, where a shifted copy would double the joints;
  `on` forces it and `off` disables it. An opacity cutout is never doubled;
- varies brightness and roughness in patches about a metre across (with `--mapping uv` the size follows
  the UV layout) and widens the roughness range (`--no-variation` turns this off, e.g. for a clean,
  factory-new surface).

## Relief that reads

- Where the camera is close to the surface, displace the geometry (`--true-displacement`) and dice it with a
  Subdivision Surface modifier: `use_adaptive_subdivision = True`, `adaptive_space = "PIXEL"`,
  `adaptive_pixel_size = 1` (Cycles only). Keep that modifier last in the stack: with any modifier after it,
  only its fixed levels are used and a plane renders flat. Then set the material's `displacement_method` to
  `"DISPLACEMENT"` (`"BOTH"` only while dicing is coarse; the default `"BUMP"` moves no geometry).

## Variation strength

A raw roughness map gives one even sheen and a raw colour map one even tone. To tune the built-in
variation against a reference, edit the Map Range nodes labelled `large-scale value noise` (brightness
multiplier, 0.92-1.08), `large-scale roughness noise` (added roughness, ±0.05) and `roughness range`
(spread ×1.2). Keep them subtle: stronger settings read as blotches or smudges, not wear.

# Scattered detail

In Geometry Nodes, vary scale per axis by feeding a Random Value (Vector) into Instance on Points'
Scale. This builds the scatter with independent per-axis scale, roll, a small lift and clustered density, for a
prototype modelled with its length along X:

```python
import bpy

def scatter(host, proto, per_cm2=4.0, clusters=4.0, seed=0):
    """Instances of proto over host's upward faces, varied in size, tilt, spacing and colour.

    per_cm2: instances per square centimetre before the clumping thins them to about half, with the
    scene in metres. clusters: clumps across the host's width.
    """
    tree = bpy.data.node_groups.new(f"{host.name}Scatter", "GeometryNodeTree")
    tree.interface.new_socket("Geometry", in_out="OUTPUT", socket_type="NodeSocketGeometry")
    n, link = tree.nodes, tree.links.new
    group_out = n.new("NodeGroupOutput")
    surface = n.new("GeometryNodeObjectInfo")  # the host as evaluated, modifiers included
    surface.inputs["Object"].default_value = host
    surface.transform_space = "RELATIVE"
    noise = n.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")  # low-frequency density over the surface: clumps and gaps
    noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value = clusters / max(host.dimensions)
    noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 0.0
    link(n.new("GeometryNodeInputPosition").outputs[0], noise.inputs["Vector"])
    weight = n.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
    weight.inputs["From Min"].default_value, weight.inputs["From Max"].default_value = 0.45, 0.55
    weight.inputs["To Min"].default_value = 0.1  # gaps stay sparse, never empty
    link(noise.outputs["Fac"], weight.inputs["Value"])
    up = n.new("ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ")
    link(n.new("GeometryNodeInputNormal").outputs[0], up.inputs[0])
    facing = n.new("FunctionNodeCompare")
    facing.data_type, facing.operation = "FLOAT", "GREATER_THAN"
    facing.inputs[1].default_value = 0.3
    link(up.outputs["Z"], facing.inputs[0])
    distribute = n.new("GeometryNodeDistributePointsOnFaces")
    distribute.inputs["Density"].default_value = per_cm2 * 10000
    distribute.inputs["Seed"].default_value = seed
    link(surface.outputs["Geometry"], distribute.inputs["Mesh"])
    link(facing.outputs[0], distribute.inputs["Selection"])  # per face: only upward faces
    keep = n.new("FunctionNodeRandomValue")  # per point: keep with the clump weight's probability
    keep.data_type = "BOOLEAN"
    keep.inputs["Seed"].default_value = seed + 3
    link(weight.outputs[0], keep.inputs["Probability"])
    drop = n.new("FunctionNodeBooleanMath")
    drop.operation = "NOT"
    link(keep.outputs["Value"], drop.inputs[0])
    thin = n.new("GeometryNodeDeleteGeometry")
    thin.domain = "POINT"
    link(distribute.outputs["Points"], thin.inputs["Geometry"])
    link(drop.outputs[0], thin.inputs["Selection"])
    source = n.new("GeometryNodeObjectInfo")
    source.inputs["Object"].default_value = proto
    source.inputs["As Instance"].default_value = True
    instance = n.new("GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints")
    link(thin.outputs[0], instance.inputs["Points"])
    link(source.outputs["Geometry"], instance.inputs["Instance"])
    link(distribute.outputs["Rotation"], instance.inputs["Rotation"])
    size = n.new("FunctionNodeRandomValue")  # length (x) and thickness (y, z) vary separately
    size.data_type = "FLOAT_VECTOR"
    size.inputs["Min"].default_value = (0.7, 0.85, 0.85)
    size.inputs["Max"].default_value = (1.3, 1.15, 1.15)
    size.inputs["Seed"].default_value = seed + 1
    link(size.outputs["Value"], instance.inputs["Scale"])
    tilt = n.new("FunctionNodeRandomValue")  # any roll about the length (x), a lift under 7°, any yaw
    tilt.data_type = "FLOAT_VECTOR"
    tilt.inputs["Min"].default_value = (-3.1416, -0.12, 0.0)
    tilt.inputs["Max"].default_value = (3.1416, 0.12, 6.2832)
    tilt.inputs["Seed"].default_value = seed + 2
    rotate = n.new("GeometryNodeRotateInstances")  # in each instance's own space: relative to the surface
    link(instance.outputs[0], rotate.inputs["Instances"])
    link(tilt.outputs["Value"], rotate.inputs["Rotation"])
    link(rotate.outputs[0], group_out.inputs[0])
    holder = bpy.data.objects.new(f"{host.name}Scatter", bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{host.name}Scatter"))
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(holder)
    holder.modifiers.new("Scatter", "NODES").node_group = tree
    return holder
```

Keep the holder at the origin with no transform: it reads the host in place. Count the instances
(evaluate the depsgraph) and compare with how many the reference shows on the same area; change
`per_cm2`, not the instance size, to match. In a scene not built in metres, multiply `per_cm2` by
(metres per scene unit)². Give the prototype a material whose colour comes from Object Info's Random
(one value per instance) through a colour ramp with Constant interpolation and the reference's palette.

## Scene plan

[walk-sit-reach.json](walk-sit-reach.json) is the tested 12-second authored example.
It belongs to seconds 11–23 of Mikhail Nilov's
[Man Sitting on a Chair](https://www.pexels.com/video/man-sitting-on-a-chair-7778454/),
under the [Pexels license](https://www.pexels.com/license/). Source download:
`https://videos.pexels.com/video-files/7778454/7778454-hd_1080_1920_25fps.mp4`.
Voyager's FFmpeg lacks x264, so trim with the OS's H.264 encoder. The trim maps
elapsed time to original time +11 seconds. The example's source hash binds it to the recorded trim, so a new
trim has a different hash: inspect timing, then explicitly bind a copied plan to the
new source hash.

[fixed-desk.json](fixed-desk.json) is a simpler 4.6-second seated example from
Ron Lach’s [desk recording](https://www.pexels.com/video/a-man-trying-to-remove-a-barricade-tape-9831125/),
under the same Pexels license. Download `https://videos.pexels.com/video-files/9831125/9831125-hd_2048_1080_25fps.mp4`,
then trim 4.6 seconds from 3.4 seconds. This avoids the opening far-arm occlusion.

Fields (`voyager.scene-plan/1`):

- `source_sha256`: optional source-video binding, checked when present.
- `source_yaw_degrees`: explicit constant heading calibration of the source, in
  degrees. Applied before retargeting; independent of the authored room heading.
- `smoothing`: optional `{sigma_seconds: 0.08, pole_sigma_seconds: 0.14}`, applied
  before authored corrections. Widths are standard deviations in
  seconds (0.01–0.25).
  The same option stabilizes IK bend guides and eases contact ramps. Authored foot
  paths use forward knee guides instead of noisy observed knees. Optional `repair_gap_seconds` permits bounded interpolation of missing whole poses;
  the report lists every repaired time.
- `smooth_authored_paths`: optional smooth interpolation for root and
  override paths. Holds and contact locations stay fixed. Existing jump paths
  are unchanged unless this option is enabled.
- `root`: ordered `{time, position: [x,y,z], yaw?}` keys covering the clip. Seconds,
  authored meters, Z up, forward −Y, yaw in degrees. Position offsets the standing
  rig, so a seated root has negative Z. This is a separate object action.
- `props`: boxes `{name, position, size}`.
- `contacts`: `{bone, start, end, blend, position, object?, rotation?}`. Bone is
  `hand_ik.L/R`, `foot_ik.L/R`, or `torso`. `blend` is the ramp duration at each end.
  Position is world-space unless `object` names a prop, then it is prop-local.
  Optional rotation is XYZ Euler degrees in the same space. Hand targets refer to
  the wrist; account for the palm's geometry when placing them on a surface.
  Torso support targets the center of the fixture's pelvis bone.
- `overrides`: `{bone, keys: [{time, position}]}` supplies explicitly authored
  world-space control paths, e.g. feet hidden behind furniture. It replaces location
  keys inside its interval. Include transition keys; there is no inferred blend.
- `lean_limit_degrees`: optional authored torso lean limit for scene clearance.
- `flight`: `{start,end}` intervals. Overlapping foot contacts are rejected. There
  is no floor fitting in this adapter, so the root's vertical curve survives flight.
- `reviewed_occlusions`: `{start,end,joints,reason}` acknowledges low-confidence
  landmarks after source inspection. These observations remain flagged in the report.
  Whole-pose
  loss fails unless explicitly bounded by `repair_gap_seconds`. Joint indices are MediaPipe's 33-point order.

The saved scene retains `Captured_Controls`, `Cleaned_Controls_Contacts` and the

unchanged. Select the action on the `rig` object to edit it. Contact empties are

"""Build an editable environment with a six-second camera path; preserves existing scene contents."""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))


def build(kind="forest", size=120, seed=0, style="day", cache=None, assets="cc0"):
    import bpy
    from mathutils import Vector
    from sets.builders import city, forest

    scene = bpy.context.scene
    started = time.monotonic()
    existing = set(bpy.data.objects)
    # This collection owns this invocation, so agents can move/delete an entire set.
    group = bpy.data.collections.new("Set " + kind)
    scene.collection.children.link(group)
    cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new("Set flythrough")
    camera = bpy.data.objects.new("Set camera " + kind, cam_data)
    group.objects.link(camera)
    cam_data.lens = 28 if kind in ("forest", "valley") else 24
    cam_data.clip_end = max(1000, size * 3)
    scene.camera = camera
    scene.render.resolution_x, scene.render.resolution_y = 1920, 1080
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100
    scene.render.fps = 24
    scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end = 1, 144
    forest_kind = kind in ("forest", "valley")
    for frame, t in ((1, 0), (144, 1)):
        y = -size * 0.36 + t * size * 0.38
        x = math.sin(y / 22) * 5 if kind == "valley" else 0.3 * math.sin(t * 2)
        z = (
            6
            if kind == "valley"
            else 1.8
            if kind == "market"
            else 2.2
            if forest_kind
            else 3.4
        )
        camera.location = (x, y, z)
        target = Vector(
            (
                x + (1.5 if forest_kind else -2),
                y + 28,
                z + (2.8 if forest_kind else 1.8 if kind == "market" else 7),
            )
        )
        camera.rotation_euler = (
            (target - camera.location).to_track_quat("-Z", "Y").to_euler()
        )
        camera.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        camera.keyframe_insert("rotation_euler", frame=frame)
    # Blender's layered actions have channel bags; keyframes default Bezier, giving a gentle ease.
    scene.frame_set(1)
    result = (
        forest(size, seed, camera, cache, assets, kind == "valley")
        if forest_kind
        else city(kind, size, seed, style, cache, assets)
    )
    for obj in set(bpy.data.objects) - existing:
        if obj == camera or not obj.users_collection:
            continue
        # Source collections stay unlinked: only carrier geometry is visible in the set.
        if any(c == scene.collection for c in obj.users_collection):
            scene.collection.objects.unlink(obj)
            group.objects.link(obj)
    group["set_type"] = kind
    group["seed"] = seed
    group["style"] = style
    result.update(
        {
            "type": kind,
            "size_m": size,
            "seed": seed,
            "style": style,
            "collection": group.name,
            "camera": camera.name,
            "objects": len(group.objects),
            "frames": 144,
            "fps": 24,
            "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
        }
    )
    return result


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=__doc__,
        epilog="Example: blender -b --factory-startup --python build-set.py -- --type downtown --size 160 --style night --save downtown.blend. Geometry and emissive materials only; apply look.py beside this script to add lighting/atmosphere. Size is the set width in meters. Existing objects are preserved; a named Set collection owns the new geometry. Camera is replaced as the active scene camera. Uses CPU-compatible native Blender nodes.",
    )

    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument(

    parser.add_argument(

if __name__ == "__main__":

    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - CLI boundary: report one line and exit nonzero
