"""Compare how each object in a render looks against the user's reference image, before showing the render.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python compare-reference.py -- \\
        --reference REF --render RENDER --out review/compare.png --object NAME=X,Y,W,H[/X,Y,W,H] ... \\
        [--mask NAME=REF_MASK] [--render-mask NAME=RENDER_MASK] [--grid]

Compare the PNG or JPEG still the user will see: an EXR is measured without the scene's view transform.

Each --object names one object or surface and its box on the reference, as fractions of the frame from
the top-left corner (0.6,0.55,0.4,0.45 is the bottom-right); a second box after ``/`` is its box on the
render when the framing differs. --crop is an older name for --object. Both boxes are scaled to one
height, shown side by side in OUT-<NAME>.png, and stacked for every object in OUT-objects.png.

An object with plain background around it in its box is measured on its own pixels (the sheet dims the
rest); otherwise the whole box is, so a box inside a surface measures that surface. An object line ends
with [measured on ...] when it was measured otherwise: on a given mask, or on the whole box because the
outline was found on one side only. When the object is not found (a dark mug on a dark wall), --mask
gives it on the reference and --render-mask on the render: a full-frame image, white or opaque on the
object; a side without a mask borrows the other's. A render mask is a still of the scene with Film >
Transparent on and every other object's visible_camera off: its alpha is the object. A hard light/shadow edge across a box is reported as
light, and highlights, texture and contrast are then read inside one side of it. The look is
compared aspect by aspect: colour (hue, saturation, value, warmth), highlights (size, strength,
sharpness), texture (fine and broad detail, grain scale, tiling), contrast (tonal range, shadow depth)
and edges (outline sharpness, glow, light passing through). Output opens with one
``COMPARE_OBJECT <name>: ...`` line per object, naming each gap and the change that closes it, then a
``COMPARE_REFERENCE_FRAME (advisory)`` line (framing, whole-frame and regional tone checks) and a
``COMPARE_REFERENCE_JSON`` line with every number; OUT.json holds the same, OUT the two whole frames
side by side. --grid also writes OUT-grid.png with lines every 10%, for reading boxes and positions.
Transparent pixels are measured over mid grey. An object given its own render box says where the camera
differs and decides framing; else the whole frame's layout does, and a layout that no zoom or shift improves
is "unclear" (light and tone also move it), not "differs".

Findings are prompts to look, not verdicts: a stylized brief may differ on purpose. A comparison that
runs exits 0 whatever it finds; every failure prints ``compare-reference: error: ...`` and exits non-zero.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True  # no __pycache__ left in the skill folder
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))  # object_look.py sits beside this script
from object_look import compare_object, resample, resize

DETAIL_HEIGHT = 256
SHEET_HEIGHT = 900
CROP_HEIGHT = 512
GAP = 12
# Loose tolerances, render vs reference: beyond them the difference is usually visible side by side.
ASPECT_TOLERANCE = 0.02
LUMINANCE_TOLERANCE = 0.08
SATURATION_TOLERANCE = 0.08
CONTRAST_RATIO = (0.75, 1.33)
DETAIL_RATIO = (0.6, 1.6)
# Regional tone: mean luminance of a TONE_GRID x TONE_GRID grid, and the frame's darkest and brightest tenth.
TONE_GRID = 3
REGION_TOLERANCE = 0.1
TONE_GRID_NAMES = (("top left", "top", "top right"), ("left", "middle", "right"), ("bottom left", "bottom", "bottom right"))
MASK_MIN_COVER = 0.01  # a given mask must cover this share of its object's box
CONTACT_ROW_HEIGHT = 240
CONTACT_WIDTH = 1200
# Framing (advisory): correlation of LAYOUT_SIZE square normalized luminance maps; the search zooms the render by
# LAYOUT_SCALES and shifts it by LAYOUT_SHIFTS (fractions of the frame) for its best alignment.
LAYOUT_SIZE = 32
LAYOUT_WORKING = 192
LAYOUT_CORRELATION = 0.8
LAYOUT_UNRELATED = 0.3  # below it the frames share little layout: another view or other content
LAYOUT_SCALES = [round(1.06 ** step, 4) for step in range(-7, 8)]
LAYOUT_SHIFTS = [step / 32 for step in range(-8, 9)]
LAYOUT_MIN_OVERLAP = 0.4
# A zoom or shift is named only when it beats the frame as rendered by LAYOUT_GAIN, lines the two up to
# LAYOUT_ALIGNED and is inside the searched range: a poor best fit is a different layout, not a direction.
LAYOUT_GAIN = 0.05
LAYOUT_ALIGNED = 0.75
LAYOUT_SCALE_STEP = 0.1
LAYOUT_SHIFT_STEP = 0.06
# Objects given a separate render box sit elsewhere in the render; off by OBJECT_SHIFT of the frame or
# OBJECT_SCALE in size, framing fails.
OBJECT_SHIFT = 0.03
OBJECT_SCALE = 0.1


class CompareError(Exception):
    pass


def parse_box(text):
    try:
        values = [float(part) for part in text.split(",")]
    except ValueError:
        raise CompareError(f"box {text!r} is not four numbers")
    if len(values) != 4 or not all(math.isfinite(value) for value in values):
        raise CompareError(f"box {text!r} needs four finite numbers X,Y,W,H")
    x, y, w, h = values
    if w <= 0 or h <= 0 or x < 0 or y < 0 or x + w > 1.0001 or y + h > 1.0001:
        raise CompareError(f"box {text!r} must lie inside the frame (fractions 0-1 from the top-left)")
    return x, y, w, h


def parse_object(text):
    name, sep, boxes = text.partition("=")
    if not sep or not name or not name.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
        raise CompareError(f"--object {text!r} needs NAME=X,Y,W,H[/X,Y,W,H] with a plain name")
    first, _, second = boxes.partition("/")
    reference = parse_box(first)
    return name, reference, parse_box(second) if second else reference


def parse_mask(option, text, names):
    name, sep, path = text.partition("=")
    if not sep or name not in names or not path:
        raise CompareError(f"{option} {text!r} needs NAME=MASK_FILE naming an --object")
    return name, path


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise CompareError(message)


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = Parser(prog="compare-reference.py", allow_abbrev=False)
    parser.add_argument("--reference", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--render", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="side-by-side PNG; crops and JSON are written next to it")
    # --crop is the older name: a crop is an object box.
    parser.add_argument("--object", "--crop", dest="objects", action="append", default=[], help="NAME=X,Y,W,H[/X,Y,W,H]")
    parser.add_argument("--mask", dest="masks", action="append", default=[], help="NAME=REF_MASK, the object on the reference")
    parser.add_argument("--render-mask", dest="render_masks", action="append", default=[], help="NAME=RENDER_MASK, the object on the render")
    parser.add_argument("--grid", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    args.objects = [parse_object(text) for text in args.objects]
    # Two options rather than one with a separator: a separator would also split the paths.
    objects = {name for name, _, _ in args.objects}
    sides = [dict(parse_mask(option, text, objects) for text in texts) for option, texts in (("--mask", args.masks), ("--render-mask", args.render_masks))]
    args.masks = {name: [side.get(name) for side in sides] for name in objects if any(name in side for side in sides)}
    # Folded: on a case-insensitive disk, Mug and mug, or Objects and the contact sheet, are one file.
    names = {name.casefold() for name, _, _ in args.objects}
    if len(names) != len(args.objects):
        raise CompareError("object names must be unique")
    if {"objects", "grid"} & names:
        raise CompareError("object names 'objects' and 'grid' are taken by the contact and grid sheets")
    return args


def load(bpy, np, path):
    """An image file as a float array, rows top to bottom, RGB in display (sRGB) values 0-1."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise CompareError(f"{path} does not exist")
    try:
        image = bpy.data.images.load(os.path.abspath(path), check_existing=False)
    except RuntimeError as error:
        raise CompareError(f"{path} is not an image Blender can read ({error})")
    width, height = image.size
    if width == 0 or height == 0:
        raise CompareError(f"{path} has no pixels")
    pixels = np.empty(width * height * 4, dtype=np.float32)
    image.pixels.foreach_get(pixels)
    rgba = pixels.reshape(height, width, 4)[::-1]
    rgb, alpha = rgba[:, :, :3], rgba[:, :, 3:]
    if image.is_float:
        # A float buffer (EXR, 16-bit PNG) holds premultiplied linear values; a byte buffer holds the
        # file's straight sRGB values. Bring both to straight sRGB, as a viewer shows them.
        rgb = np.clip(np.where(alpha > 1e-6, rgb / np.maximum(alpha, 1e-6), 0), 0, 1)
        rgb = np.where(rgb <= 0.0031308, rgb * 12.92, 1.055 * np.power(rgb, 1 / 2.4) - 0.055)
    bpy.data.images.remove(image)
    rgb = np.clip(rgb, 0, 1) * alpha + 0.5 * (1 - alpha)  # over mid grey, so transparency measures the same
    return np.ascontiguousarray(np.clip(rgb, 0, 1).astype(np.float32))


def load_mask(bpy, np, path, shape):
    """A mask image as booleans at an image's size: its alpha where the alpha varies (a transparent render),
    else its brightness (white is the object)."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise CompareError(f"mask {path} does not exist")
    try:
        image = bpy.data.images.load(os.path.abspath(path), check_existing=False)
    except RuntimeError as error:
        raise CompareError(f"mask {path} is not an image Blender can read ({error})")
    width, height = image.size
    pixels = np.empty(width * height * 4, dtype=np.float32)
    image.pixels.foreach_get(pixels)
    bpy.data.images.remove(image)
    rgba = pixels.reshape(height, width, 4)[::-1]
    alpha = rgba[:, :, 3]
    value = alpha if alpha.max() - alpha.min() > 0.5 else rgba[:, :, :3].mean(axis=2)
    if abs(width / height - shape[1] / shape[0]) > ASPECT_TOLERANCE * shape[1] / shape[0]:
        raise CompareError(f"mask {path} is {width}x{height}, not the shape of the {shape[1]}x{shape[0]} image it masks")
    return resample(np, resample(np, value, 0, shape[0]), 1, shape[1]) > 0.5


def crop(rgb, box):
    height, width = rgb.shape[:2]
    x, y, w, h = box
    left, top = int(round(x * width)), int(round(y * height))
    right, bottom = min(int(round((x + w) * width)), width), min(int(round((y + h) * height)), height)
    if right - left < 8 or bottom - top < 8:
        raise CompareError(f"crop box {box} covers under 8 pixels of a {width}x{height} image")
    return rgb[top:bottom, left:right]


def measure_pair(np, reference, render):
    """Both images measured at one shared height, never enlarged: enlarging adds no detail and shrinking
    averages contrast and grain away, so measuring at different scales would report the same content
    as different."""
    height = min(DETAIL_HEIGHT, reference.shape[0], render.shape[0])
    return measure(np, reference, height), measure(np, render, height)


def measure(np, image, height):
    rgb = resize(np, image, height)
    luminance = rgb @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722], dtype=np.float32)
    high, low = rgb.max(axis=2), rgb.min(axis=2)
    saturation = np.where(high > 1e-4, (high - low) / np.maximum(high, 1e-4), 0)
    if luminance.shape[0] < 3 or luminance.shape[1] < 3:
        detail = 0.0
    else:
        lum = luminance
        laplacian = 4 * lum[1:-1, 1:-1] - lum[:-2, 1:-1] - lum[2:, 1:-1] - lum[1:-1, :-2] - lum[1:-1, 2:]
        detail = float(np.abs(laplacian).mean())
    return {
        "size": [int(image.shape[1]), int(image.shape[0])],
        "aspect": round(image.shape[1] / image.shape[0], 4),
        "meanRgb": [round(float(value) * 255) for value in rgb.reshape(-1, 3).mean(axis=0)],
        "luminance": round(float(luminance.mean()), 4),
        "contrast": round(float(luminance.std()), 4),
        "saturation": round(float(saturation.mean()), 4),
        "warmth": round(float((rgb[:, :, 0] - rgb[:, :, 2]).mean()), 4),
        "detail": round(detail, 5),
    }


def checks(reference, render, whole):
    found = []
    if whole and abs(render["aspect"] / reference["aspect"] - 1) > ASPECT_TOLERANCE:
        found.append(f"aspect {render['aspect']} vs {reference['aspect']}: render the reference's aspect and framing")
    if abs(render["luminance"] - reference["luminance"]) > LUMINANCE_TOLERANCE:
        side = "brighter" if render["luminance"] > reference["luminance"] else "darker"
        found.append(f"luminance {render['luminance']} vs {reference['luminance']}: render is {side}")
    if abs(render["saturation"] - reference["saturation"]) > SATURATION_TOLERANCE:
        side = "more" if render["saturation"] > reference["saturation"] else "less"
        found.append(f"saturation {render['saturation']} vs {reference['saturation']}: render is {side} saturated")
    for key, (low, high), flat, busy in (
        ("contrast", CONTRAST_RATIO, "flatter", "harsher"),
        ("detail", DETAIL_RATIO, "smoother (texture, grain or relief missing or blurred)", "busier"),
    ):
        if reference[key] > 0:
            ratio = render[key] / reference[key]
            if ratio < low or ratio > high:
                found.append(f"{key} {render[key]} vs {reference[key]}: render is {flat if ratio < low else busy}")
    return found


def tone_checks(np, reference, render):
    """Large-area tone: the frame's darkest and brightest tenth, and the mean of each cell of a grid, which
    a whole-frame mean averages away (a dark table beside a bright plate)."""
    luminance = [resize(np, image, LAYOUT_WORKING) @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722], dtype=np.float32) for image in (reference, render)]
    found = []
    for name, percent in (("darkest tenth", 10), ("brightest tenth", 90)):
        target, rendered = (float(np.percentile(values, percent)) for values in luminance)
        if abs(rendered - target) > LUMINANCE_TOLERANCE:
            found.append(f"tone: {name} at {rendered:.2f} vs {target:.2f}: render's {'shadows' if percent == 10 else 'highlights'} are {'brighter' if rendered > target else 'darker'}")
    cells = [resample(np, resample(np, values, 0, TONE_GRID), 1, TONE_GRID) for values in luminance]
    for row in range(TONE_GRID):
        for column in range(TONE_GRID):
            target, rendered = float(cells[0][row, column]), float(cells[1][row, column])
            if abs(rendered - target) > REGION_TOLERANCE:
                found.append(f"tone: {TONE_GRID_NAMES[row][column]} of the frame {'brighter' if rendered > target else 'darker'} ({rendered:.2f} vs {target:.2f})")
    return found


def object_framing(objects):
    """Notes on objects whose render box sits elsewhere than their reference box: the boxes say where the
    camera differs. A render box of another shape marks a patch, not the object's extent, so only its centre counts."""
    notes = []
    for name, reference_box, render_box in objects:
        if render_box == reference_box:
            continue
        shift_x = (render_box[0] + render_box[2] / 2) - (reference_box[0] + reference_box[2] / 2)
        shift_y = (render_box[1] + render_box[3] / 2) - (reference_box[1] + reference_box[3] / 2)
        scale = render_box[3] / reference_box[3]
        same_shape = abs((render_box[2] / reference_box[2]) / scale - 1) <= OBJECT_SCALE
        words = [f"{abs(value):.0%} {positive if value > 0 else negative}" for value, positive, negative in
                 ((shift_x, "right", "left"), (shift_y, "lower", "higher")) if abs(value) >= OBJECT_SHIFT]
        if same_shape and abs(scale - 1) > OBJECT_SCALE:
            words.append(f"{scale:.2f}x the size")
        if words:
            notes.append(f"{name} sits {', '.join(words)} in the render (from its render box)")
    return notes


def dim_outside(np, rgb, mask):
    """The crop with what was not measured as the object dimmed, so a wrong mask shows on the sheet."""
    if mask.all():
        return rgb
    inside = resample(np, resample(np, mask.astype(np.float32), 0, rgb.shape[0]), 1, rgb.shape[1]) > 0.5
    return np.where(inside[:, :, None], rgb, rgb * 0.35)


def compare_framing(np, reference, render, object_notes=()):
    """Layout: both frames shrunk to LAYOUT_SIZE square luminance maps, each normalized to zero mean and
    unit spread so exposure and contrast do not count, and correlated. Then the render map is zoomed and
    shifted to find where it lines up best: that says which way the camera is off."""
    size = LAYOUT_SIZE
    target, rendered = layout_map(np, reference, size), layout_map(np, render, size)
    # Two flat frames (one plain colour each) have no layout to differ in.
    correlation = 1.0 if not target.any() and not rendered.any() else float((target * rendered).mean())
    best = (correlation, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    positions = (np.arange(size) + 0.5) / size
    # Shrunk once to a small square, so each scale's map is not another pass over a full-size still.
    small = resample(np, resample(np, render, 0, LAYOUT_WORKING), 1, LAYOUT_WORKING)
    for scale in LAYOUT_SCALES:
        source_size = max(2, round(size * scale))
        source = layout_map(np, small, source_size)
        # Reference position u shows render position 0.5 + (u - 0.5) / scale + shift.
        weights, valid = zip(*(sampling(np, 0.5 + (positions - 0.5) / scale + shift, source_size) for shift in LAYOUT_SHIFTS))
        weights, valid = np.stack(weights), np.stack(valid).astype(np.float32)
        # sampled[y, x] is the render map read with vertical shift y and horizontal shift x.
        sampled = np.einsum("yjm,ml->yjl", weights, source)
        sampled = np.einsum("yjm,xlm->yxjl", sampled, weights)
        mask = valid[:, None, :, None] * valid[None, :, None, :]
        count = np.maximum(mask.sum(axis=(2, 3)), 1)
        mean_t, mean_s = (target * mask).sum(axis=(2, 3)) / count, (sampled * mask).sum(axis=(2, 3)) / count
        covariance = (target * sampled * mask).sum(axis=(2, 3)) / count - mean_t * mean_s
        variance_t = (target * target * mask).sum(axis=(2, 3)) / count - mean_t ** 2
        variance_s = (sampled * sampled * mask).sum(axis=(2, 3)) / count - mean_s ** 2
        spread = np.sqrt(np.maximum(variance_t, 0) * np.maximum(variance_s, 0))
        enough = (mask.sum(axis=(2, 3)) >= LAYOUT_MIN_OVERLAP * size * size) & (spread > 1e-6)
        scores = np.where(enough, covariance / np.maximum(spread, 1e-6), -1)
        y, x = np.unravel_index(int(np.argmax(scores)), scores.shape)
        if scores[y, x] > best[0] + 1e-6:
            best = (float(scores[y, x]), float(scale), float(LAYOUT_SHIFTS[x]), float(LAYOUT_SHIFTS[y]))
    return framing_report(correlation, best, object_notes)


def layout_map(np, rgb, size):
    luminance = resample(np, resample(np, rgb, 0, size), 1, size) @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722], dtype=np.float32)
    spread = float(luminance.std())
    return (luminance - luminance.mean()) / spread if spread > 1e-3 else np.zeros_like(luminance)


def sampling(np, positions, size):
    """Linear-interpolation weights (positions x size) reading a size-pixel axis at fractional positions;
    positions outside the axis get no weight and are marked invalid."""
    pixel = np.clip(positions * size - 0.5, 0, size - 1)
    low = np.minimum(np.floor(pixel).astype(int), size - 2)
    fraction = pixel - low
    valid = (positions >= 0) & (positions <= 1)
    weights = np.zeros((len(positions), size), dtype=np.float32)
    rows = np.arange(len(positions))
    weights[rows, low] = (1 - fraction) * valid
    weights[rows, low + 1] = fraction * valid
    return weights, valid


def framing_report(correlation, best, object_notes=()):
    best_correlation, scale, shift_x, shift_y = best
    notes = []
    inside = LAYOUT_SCALES[0] < scale < LAYOUT_SCALES[-1] and max(abs(shift_x), abs(shift_y)) < LAYOUT_SHIFTS[-1]
    if best_correlation - correlation > LAYOUT_GAIN and best_correlation >= LAYOUT_ALIGNED and inside:
        if scale > 1 + LAYOUT_SCALE_STEP:
            notes.append(f"subject smaller than in the reference (about {1 / scale:.2f}x): move the camera in or lengthen the focal length")
        if scale < 1 - LAYOUT_SCALE_STEP:
            notes.append(f"subject larger than in the reference (about {1 / scale:.2f}x): move the camera back or shorten the focal length")
        for shift, positive, negative in ((shift_x, "right", "left"), (shift_y, "down", "up")):
            if abs(shift) >= LAYOUT_SHIFT_STEP:
                notes.append(f"subject shifted {positive if shift > 0 else negative} by about {abs(shift):.0%} of the frame")
    passed = correlation >= LAYOUT_CORRELATION and not notes
    if object_notes:
        return framing_entry(correlation, best, False, object_notes + notes)
    if not passed and not notes and correlation < LAYOUT_UNRELATED:
        notes.append("layout differs: the frames share little layout (another view or other content); compare object positions on the sheets")
    if not passed and not notes:
        # Nothing lines the frames up better: the layout map also follows light and tone, so a middling
        # correlation alone does not say the camera is off.
        passed = None
        notes.append("no zoom or shift lines the frames up better, so light and tone may differ rather than the camera;"
                     " give objects a render box (NAME=REF_BOX/RENDER_BOX) where they sit elsewhere")
    return framing_entry(correlation, best, passed, notes)


def framing_entry(correlation, best, passed, notes):
    best_correlation, scale, shift_x, shift_y = best
    return {
        "correlation": round(correlation, 3),
        "best": {"correlation": round(best_correlation, 3), "scale": round(scale, 3), "shiftX": round(shift_x, 3), "shiftY": round(shift_y, 3)},
        "pass": passed,
        "notes": notes,
    }


def contact_sheet(np, sheets):
    """Every object's sheet stacked, one row each, at one height unless that would make a row too wide."""
    rows = [resize(np, sheet, max(8, min(CONTACT_ROW_HEIGHT, round(CONTACT_WIDTH * sheet.shape[0] / sheet.shape[1])))) for sheet in sheets]
    width = max(row.shape[1] for row in rows)
    padded = [np.concatenate([row, np.ones((row.shape[0], width - row.shape[1], 3), dtype=np.float32)], axis=1) for row in rows]
    gap = np.ones((GAP, width, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    return np.concatenate([part for row in padded for part in (row, gap)][:-1], axis=0)


def object_line(name, entry):
    # Said only when it is not the usual reading (the object's own pixels, or a box drawn inside a surface).
    measured = "" if entry["measured"] in ("object", "whole box") else f" [measured on the {entry['measured']}]"
    if entry["measured"].startswith("whole box:"):
        measured = f" [measured on the {entry['measured']}; pass --mask {name}=... or --render-mask {name}=... to measure the object alone]"
    if not entry["findings"]:
        return f"COMPARE_OBJECT {name}: look matches the reference{measured}"
    return f"COMPARE_OBJECT {name}: {len(entry['findings'])} look gap{'s' if len(entry['findings']) > 1 else ''} | " + " | ".join(entry["findings"]) + measured


def frame_line(report):
    framing = report["framing"]
    verdict = {True: "matches", False: "differs", None: "unclear"}[framing["pass"]]
    parts = [f"framing {verdict} (layout {framing['correlation']})" + "".join(f"; {note}" for note in framing["notes"])]
    parts.append(f"whole frame {len(report['checks'])} checks" + "".join(f"; {check}" for check in report["checks"]))
    return "COMPARE_REFERENCE_FRAME (advisory) " + " | ".join(parts)


def side_by_side(np, left, right, height, decorate=lambda image: image):
    left, right = decorate(resize(np, left, height)), decorate(resize(np, right, height))
    gap = np.ones((height, GAP, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    return np.concatenate([left, gap, right], axis=1)


def with_grid(np, rgb):
    out = rgb.copy()
    height, width = out.shape[:2]
    for step in range(1, 10):
        colour = np.array([1.0, 0.2, 0.2] if step == 5 else [0.2, 0.9, 1.0], dtype=np.float32)
        thickness = 3 if step == 5 else 1
        x, y = round(width * step / 10), round(height * step / 10)
        out[:, max(0, x - thickness // 2):x + thickness - thickness // 2] = colour
        out[max(0, y - thickness // 2):y + thickness - thickness // 2, :] = colour
    return out


def save(bpy, np, rgb, path):
    height, width = rgb.shape[:2]
    image = bpy.data.images.new(os.path.basename(path), width, height, alpha=False)
    rgba = np.ones((height, width, 4), dtype=np.float32)
    rgba[:, :, :3] = rgb
    image.pixels.foreach_set(rgba[::-1].ravel())
    image.filepath_raw = os.path.abspath(path)
    image.file_format = "PNG"
    image.save()
    bpy.data.images.remove(image)


def main(argv):
    try:
        import bpy
        import numpy as np
    except ImportError:
        raise CompareError("run this under Blender: blender -b --factory-startup --python compare-reference.py -- ...")
    args = parse_args(argv)
    reference, render = load(bpy, np, args.reference), load(bpy, np, args.render)
    out = os.path.abspath(args.out)
    stem = out[:-4] if out.lower().endswith(".png") else out
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
    height = min(SHEET_HEIGHT, max(reference.shape[0], render.shape[0]))
    save(bpy, np, side_by_side(np, reference, render, height), stem + ".png")
    measured = measure_pair(np, reference, render)
    report = {"sheet": stem + ".png", "reference": measured[0], "render": measured[1], "objects": {}}
    report["checks"] = checks(report["reference"], report["render"], whole=True) + tone_checks(np, reference, render)
    report["framing"] = compare_framing(np, reference, render, object_framing(args.objects))
    if args.grid:
        report["grid"] = stem + "-grid.png"
        # Grid drawn after resizing, so its lines keep their colour on large images.
        save(bpy, np, side_by_side(np, reference, render, height, decorate=lambda image: with_grid(np, image)), report["grid"])
    sheets = []
    for name, reference_box, render_box in args.objects:
        left, right = crop(reference, reference_box), crop(render, render_box)
        given = [None if path is None else crop(load_mask(bpy, np, path, image.shape[:2])[:, :, None], box)[:, :, 0]
                 for path, image, box in zip(args.masks.get(name, (None, None)), (reference, render), (reference_box, render_box))]
        # An off box or the wrong file leaves (nearly) nothing to measure.
        if any(mask is not None and mask.mean() < MASK_MIN_COVER for mask in given):
            raise CompareError(f"a mask for {name} covers under {MASK_MIN_COVER:.0%} of its box: check the mask file and the box")
        compared, masks = compare_object(np, left, right, given)
        sheets.append(side_by_side(np, dim_outside(np, left, masks[0]), dim_outside(np, right, masks[1]), CROP_HEIGHT))
        entry = {"sheet": f"{stem}-{name}.png", **compared}
        save(bpy, np, sheets[-1], entry["sheet"])
        report["objects"][name] = entry
    if sheets:
        report["contact"] = stem + "-objects.png"
        save(bpy, np, contact_sheet(np, sheets), report["contact"])
    lines = [object_line(name, entry) for name, entry in report["objects"].items()] or [
        "COMPARE_OBJECT none: name each key object with --object NAME=X,Y,W,H[/X,Y,W,H] to compare its look"
    ]
    report["summary"] = lines + [frame_line(report)]
    with open(stem + ".json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(report, handle, indent=2)
    print("\n".join(report["summary"]), flush=True)
    print("COMPARE_REFERENCE_JSON " + json.dumps(report), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    try:
        main(argv)
    except Exception as error:  # every failure, not only ours, must exit non-zero: Blender exits 0 after a traceback
        message = str(error) if isinstance(error, CompareError) else f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
        print(f"compare-reference: error: {message}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        sys.exit(1)

"""Extract original MediaPipe observations; no downloads or Blender dependency."""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import time

for name in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ.setdefault(name, "2")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("video", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--max-frames", type=int, default=1800)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.max_frames <= 0:
        parser.error("--max-frames must be positive")
    os.environ.setdefault("MPLCONFIGDIR", str(args.output.parent.resolve() / ".matplotlib"))
    import av
    import mediapipe

    start = time.monotonic()
    options = mediapipe.tasks.vision.PoseLandmarkerOptions(
        base_options=mediapipe.tasks.BaseOptions(
            model_asset_path=str(args.model), delegate=mediapipe.tasks.BaseOptions.Delegate.CPU
        ),
        running_mode=mediapipe.tasks.vision.RunningMode.VIDEO,
        num_poses=1,
    )
    with (
        av.open(str(args.video)) as video,
        mediapipe.tasks.vision.PoseLandmarker.create_from_options(options) as pose,
        args.output.open("x") as output,
    ):
        stream = video.streams.video[0]
        stream.codec_context.thread_count = 2
        header = {
            "type": "header",
            "schema": "voyager.pose/1",
            "source": str(args.video.resolve()),
            "source_sha256": digest(args.video),
            "model_sha256": digest(args.model),
            "mediapipe": mediapipe.__version__,
            "model_file": args.model.name,
            "mode": "VIDEO",
            "delegate": "CPU",
            "coordinate_system": "MediaPipe: x right, y down, z away; world hip-relative estimated meters; no world root translation",
            "landmark_fields": ["x", "y", "z", "visibility", "presence"],
            "width": stream.width,
            "height": stream.height,
            "nominal_fps": str(stream.average_rate),
            "time_base": str(stream.time_base),
            "max_frames": args.max_frames,
        }
        output.write(json.dumps(header) + "\n")
        first = None
        previous_ms = -1
        count = missing = 0
        end = 0
        for frame in video.decode(stream):
            if count >= args.max_frames:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Frame budget exceeded; trim the input or explicitly increase --max-frames. Output is incomplete (no summary)."
                )
            if (
                any(side.type.name == "DISPLAYMATRIX" for side in frame.side_data)
                or stream.metadata.get("rotate", "0") != "0"
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Rotated video: normalize orientation with FFmpeg first and retain source timing/provenance"
                )
            if frame.pts is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Missing presentation timestamp; prepare a timestamped source first"
                )
            timestamp = float(frame.pts * frame.time_base)
            if first is None:
                first = timestamp
            elapsed = timestamp - first
            millis = round(elapsed * 1000)
            if millis <= previous_ms:
                raise ValueError("Timestamps are not strictly increasing at millisecond precision")
            previous_ms = millis
            result = pose.detect_for_video(
                mediapipe.Image(
                    image_format=mediapipe.ImageFormat.SRGB, data=frame.to_ndarray(format="rgb24")
                ),
                millis,
            )
            record = {
                "type": "frame",
                "index": count,
                "pts": frame.pts,
                "time_base": str(frame.time_base),
                "duration_ticks": frame.duration,
                "source_seconds": timestamp,
                "seconds": elapsed,
                "inference_ms": millis,
                "image": landmarks(result.pose_landmarks),
                "world": landmarks(result.pose_world_landmarks),
            }
            output.write(json.dumps(record, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
            count += 1
            missing += not bool(record["world"])
            end = elapsed + (
                float(frame.duration * frame.time_base)
                if frame.duration
                else 1 / float(stream.average_rate)
            )
        if not count:
            raise ValueError("No video frames decoded")
        summary = {
            "type": "summary",
            "frames": count,
            "missing": missing,
            "duration_seconds": end,
            "wall_seconds": time.monotonic() - start,
        }
        output.write(json.dumps(summary) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(summary))


def digest(path):
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        return hashlib.file_digest(source, "sha256").hexdigest()


def landmarks(poses):
    return [[p.x, p.y, p.z, p.visibility, p.presence] for p in poses[0]] if poses else None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Fetch a CC0 scanned material (Poly Haven texture, ambientCG material) or a Poly Haven HDRI into the
project, wire it into a .blend, and record its credit.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python fetch-material.py -- --blend scene.blend \\
        --world "studio" --material "Table=oak wood" --material "Floor,Wall=concrete"    (several in one call)
    blender -b --factory-startup --python fetch-material.py -- --blend scene.blend \\
        (--asset ID | --search "rusty metal") [--source poly-haven|ambientcg] [--hdri] [--objects Cube,Table] \\
        [--resolution 2k] [--tile-size M] [--mapping box|uv] [--anti-tiling auto|on|off] [--no-variation] \\
        [--true-displacement] [--strength 1 --rotation 0]

A material lands in <project>/textures/<id>/ and becomes a Principled BSDF (colour sRGB; roughness, metalness,
AO and opacity Non-Color; displacement as bump) on --objects. Mapping "box" (default, needs no UVs) projects
on object coordinates so one tile covers the scan's real size (--tile-size, metres, overrides) and keeps that size
when the object is scaled later; "uv" uses the UV map once per UV square and adds the OpenGL normal map.
By default every map but an opacity cutout is sampled twice, the second copy turned 180 degrees and shifted,
and blended through a noise mask so repeats do not show (--anti-tiling; auto skips laid patterns such as bricks,
tiles and planks), and noise in patches about a metre across (with UVs, per UV square as one tile) varies
brightness and roughness, whose range is widened (--no-variation turns that off). An HDRI lands in <project>/hdri/<id>/ and becomes the world (--strength,
--rotation degrees about Z). <project> is the .blend's folder unless --project.
--world TERMS (an HDRI) and --material OBJECTS=TERMS (repeatable) fetch and wire several assets in one call; TERMS is
an asset id or search words. A search takes the scan holding every word, else the one holding the most (at least
half) with a warning.
The .blend is saved. <id>.json beside the files records source, license, credit and files; the run prints
one ``FETCH_MATERIAL_JSON `` line. Without network under Blender, run plain python3 with --download-only
first; it prints the Blender command, which reuses the downloaded files. Failures print
``fetch-material: error: ...`` and exit non-zero.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import math
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys
import urllib.parse
import zipfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("fetch_model", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "fetch-model.py"))
fetch = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(fetch)
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("material_nodes", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "material-nodes.py"))
shading = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(shading)
FetchError = fetch.FetchError

POLY_HAVEN = "https://api.polyhaven.com"
AMBIENTCG = "https://ambientcg.com/api/v3/assets"
OFFLINE_HINT = (
    "Without network access (e.g. Codex's sandbox), run the same command with plain `python3 fetch-material.py "
    "--download-only ...` with network permission; it prints the Blender command to run next."
)
# fetch-model's download errors name this script's offline step instead of its own.
fetch.OFFLINE_HINT = OFFLINE_HINT
ROLES = ("color", "roughness", "metalness", "normal", "displacement", "ao", "opacity")
# Poly Haven /files keys per role; a texture without "Diffuse" has colour variants (col_1, coll1...); the first wins.
POLY_HAVEN_MAPS = {"color": "Diffuse", "roughness": "Rough", "metalness": "Metal", "normal": "nor_gl",
                   "displacement": "Displacement", "ao": "AO"}
# ambientCG zip members end in _<Map>.jpg|png; NormalGL is the OpenGL normal Blender expects (not NormalDX).
AMBIENTCG_MAPS = {"color": "Color", "roughness": "Roughness", "metalness": "Metalness", "normal": "NormalGL",
                  "displacement": "Displacement", "ao": "AmbientOcclusion", "opacity": "Opacity"}
SOURCES = ("poly-haven", "ambientcg")
# Laid patterns whose joints a shifted second sample would double; anti-tiling "auto" leaves them single.
REGULAR_PATTERNS = {"brick", "tile", "plank", "parquet", "paving", "herringbone", "laminate", "deck", "shingle", "panel",
                    "fence", "grate", "mosaic", "chevron", "floorboard"}
TAG_PATTERNS = {"brick", "tile", "plank", "parquet", "paving", "herringbone", "mosaic", "chevron", "floorboard"}


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="fetch-material.py", allow_abbrev=False)
    what = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    what.add_argument("--asset", help="Poly Haven id (rusty_metal_02) or ambientCG id (Bricks076C)")
    what.add_argument("--search", help="Keywords, matched as whole words; the best match wins, others are listed")
    parser.add_argument("--world", help="HDRI id or search words for the world, alongside any --material")
    parser.add_argument("--material", action="append", default=[], metavar="OBJECTS=TERMS",
                        help="Objects (comma-separated) and the material id or search words for them; repeatable")
    parser.add_argument("--source", choices=SOURCES, help="Default: Poly Haven, then ambientCG")
    parser.add_argument("--hdri", action="store_true", help="Search HDRIs (Poly Haven) instead of materials")
    parser.add_argument("--blend", help="The .blend to wire and save")
    parser.add_argument("--project", help="Folder for textures/ and hdri/ (default: the .blend's folder)")
    parser.add_argument("--objects", default="", help="Comma-separated objects that get the material")
    parser.add_argument("--resolution", choices=("1k", "2k", "4k", "8k"), default="2k")
    parser.add_argument("--tile-size", type=float, help="Metres one texture tile covers (box mapping)")
    parser.add_argument("--mapping", choices=("box", "uv"), default="box")
    parser.add_argument("--anti-tiling", choices=("auto", "on", "off"), default="auto",
                        help="Blend a turned, shifted second sample to hide repeats; auto skips bricks, tiles and planks")
    parser.add_argument("--variation", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=True,
                        help="Large-scale brightness and roughness variation and a wider roughness range")
    parser.add_argument("--true-displacement", action="store_true", help="Displace geometry (needs a dense mesh)")
    parser.add_argument("--strength", type=float, default=1.0, help="HDRI strength")
    parser.add_argument("--rotation", type=float, default=0.0, help="HDRI rotation about Z, degrees")
    parser.add_argument("--max-mb", type=float, default=1024, help="Download size limit")
    parser.add_argument("--download-only", action="store_true", help="Download and stop (no Blender)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not (args.asset or args.search or args.world or args.material):
        parser.error("pass --asset or --search, or --world and/or --material")
    for entry in args.material:
        if "=" not in entry or not entry.split("=", 1)[1].strip():
            parser.error(f"--material takes OBJECTS=TERMS (e.g. \"Table,Shelf=oak wood\"), not {entry!r}")
    if args.hdri and args.source == "ambientcg":
        parser.error("--hdri fetches from Poly Haven; drop --source ambientcg")
    if not (args.blend or args.project):
        parser.error("pass --blend (or --project with --download-only)")
    if args.tile_size is not None and not 0 < args.tile_size < math.inf:
        parser.error("--tile-size must be a positive number of metres")
    return args


def main():
    args = parse_args(fetch.script_args())
    jobs = ([args] if args.asset or args.search else []) + batch_jobs(args)
    # Each job runs alone: one asset that is not found does not stop the others; the exit code reports it.
    code = max([run(job, single=len(jobs) == 1) for job in jobs])
    if args.download_only and len(jobs) > 1 and not code:
        print("Next: " + batch_next_command(args, jobs))
    return code


def batch_jobs(args):
    """One args copy per --world / --material entry, as if each had been its own call."""
    jobs = []
    for terms, objects, hdri in ([(args.world, "", True)] if args.world else []) + [
            (entry.split("=", 1)[1], entry.split("=", 1)[0], False) for entry in args.material]:
        terms = terms.strip()
        # One word that looks like an id (oak_wood_planks, Wood049) is tried as an id first, then as a search.
        as_id = terms if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", terms) and re.search(r"[_0-9]", terms) else None
        jobs.append(argparse.Namespace(**{**vars(args), "asset": as_id, "search": None if as_id else terms,
                                          "fallback_search": terms, "objects": objects, "hdri": hdri,
                                          "source": None if hdri else args.source}))
    return jobs


def run(args, single=True):
    try:
        project = os.path.abspath(args.project or os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.blend)))
        try:
            record = cached(args, project) or download(args, project)
        except FetchError:
            if not (args.asset and getattr(args, "fallback_search", None)):
                raise
            args.asset, args.search = None, args.fallback_search
            record = download(args, project)
        args.found = record["id"]
        if args.download_only:
            print("FETCH_MATERIAL_DOWNLOAD " + json.dumps(record))
            if single:
                print("Next: " + next_command(args, record))
            if single and not args.blend:
                print("Replace <scene.blend> with the saved scene the material or HDRI goes into.")
            return 0
        try:
            import bpy  # noqa: F401
        except ImportError:
            raise FetchError("run this under Blender: blender -b --factory-startup --python fetch-material.py -- ...") from None
        print("FETCH_MATERIAL_JSON " + json.dumps(apply(args, record)))
        return 0
    except FetchError as error:
        print(f"fetch-material: error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - Blender exits 0 after an uncaught script error.
        import traceback

        traceback.print_exc()
        print(f"fetch-material: error: {type(error).__name__}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


# --- Finding the asset -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def download(args, project):
    """Find the asset, download its maps into the project and write its credit record; returns the record."""
    asset = find(args)
    folder = os.path.join(project, "hdri" if asset["kind"] == "hdri" else "textures", fetch.safe_name(asset["id"]))
    max_bytes = int(args.max_mb * 2**20)
    files = (download_ambientcg(asset, folder, max_bytes) if asset["source"] == "ambientcg"
             else download_poly_haven(asset, folder, max_bytes))
    record = {key: asset[key] for key in ("source", "id", "kind", "title", "tags", "resolution", "tileSize", "alternatives",
                                            "warnings")}
    entry = fetch.registry_entry(asset["source"])
    record.update(
        sourceName=entry["name"],
        url=asset["page"],
        authors=asset["authors"],
        license=entry["license"],
        # CC0 asks for no credit; credit the scan anyway.
        attribution=f"{asset['title']}" + (f" by {', '.join(asset['authors'])}" if asset["authors"] else "")
        + f", {entry['name']} ({urllib.parse.urlparse(entry['urls']['site']).netloc}), {entry['license']}",
        folder=folder,
        files=files,
        requested=args.resolution,
        credit=os.path.join(folder, fetch.safe_name(asset["id"]) + ".json"),
    )
    with open(record["credit"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(record, handle, indent=2)
    return record


def cached(args, project):
    """The credit record of an earlier fetch of this asset at this resolution whose files are all still there."""
    if not args.asset:
        return None
    for kind in ("hdri", "textures"):
        path = os.path.join(project, kind, fetch.safe_name(args.asset), fetch.safe_name(args.asset) + ".json")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            # The folder as found now, so a moved project still finds its files.
            record = {**json.load(handle), "folder": os.path.dirname(path), "credit": path}
        complete = all(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(record["folder"], name)) for name in record["files"].values())
        if complete and record.get("requested") == args.resolution and args.source in (None, record["source"]):
            return record
    return None


def find(args):
    sources = [args.source] if args.source else ["poly-haven"] if args.hdri else list(SOURCES)
    misses, closest = [], []
    # A scan holding every search word on any source beats one holding most of them.
    for partial in ((False, True) if args.search else (False,)):
        for source in sources:
            asset = (find_ambientcg if source == "ambientcg" else find_poly_haven)(args, [] if partial else closest, partial)
            if asset:
                asset.setdefault("warnings", [])
                if partial:
                    asset["warnings"].append(f"No scan holds every word of {args.search!r}; took the closest, "
                                             f"{asset['id']} ({asset['title']}).")
                return asset
            if not partial:
                misses.append(source)
    wanted = f"--asset {args.asset!r}" if args.asset else f"--search {args.search!r}"
    nearest = f"; closest: {', '.join(closest[:8])}" if closest else ""
    hint = ". Try fewer or other words, or --asset ID" if args.search else ""
    raise FetchError(f"no {'HDRI' if args.hdri else 'material'} matches {wanted} on {' or '.join(misses)}{nearest}{hint}")


def find_poly_haven(args, closest=None, partial=False):
    if args.search:
        assets = get_json(f"{POLY_HAVEN}/assets?t={'hdris' if args.hdri else 'textures'}")
        ranked, near = poly_haven_matches(assets, args.search, partial)
        if not ranked:
            closest += [f"{other} ({assets[other]['name']}, poly-haven)" for other in near]
            return None
        asset_id, info = ranked[0], assets[ranked[0]]
        alternatives = [f"{other} ({assets[other]['name']})" for other in ranked[1:6]]
    else:
        info = get_json(f"{POLY_HAVEN}/info/{urllib.parse.quote(args.asset)}", missing_ok=True)
        if info is None:
            return None
        asset_id, alternatives = args.asset, []
    kind = {0: "hdri", 1: "material"}.get(info.get("type"))
    if kind is None:
        raise FetchError(f"Poly Haven's {asset_id!r} is a model; fetch it with fetch-model.py")
    files = get_json(f"{POLY_HAVEN}/files/{urllib.parse.quote(asset_id)}")
    listing = files.get("hdri" if kind == "hdri" else color_key(files))
    if not listing:
        raise FetchError(f"Poly Haven's {asset_id!r} lists no {'HDRI' if kind == 'hdri' else 'colour map'} "
                         f"among {', '.join(sorted(files)) or 'no files'}")
    resolution = pick_resolution(list(listing), args.resolution)
    width = (info.get("dimensions") or [0])[0] / 1000  # millimetres
    return {
        "source": "poly-haven", "id": asset_id, "kind": kind, "title": info.get("name", asset_id),
        "authors": sorted(info.get("authors") or {}), "page": f"https://polyhaven.com/a/{asset_id}",
        "resolution": resolution, "files": poly_haven_maps(files, kind, resolution),
        "alternatives": alternatives, "tags": [*info.get("tags", []), *info.get("categories", [])],
        **tile(args, width, kind),
    }


def poly_haven_matches(assets, search, partial=False):
    """(Asset ids holding every search word, best first; the closest partial matches) for a Poly Haven listing."""
    return rank(search, [(asset_id, [asset_id, info.get("name", "")], [*info.get("tags", []), *info.get("categories", [])])
                         for asset_id, info in sorted(assets.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1].get("download_count", 0))],
                partial)


def rank(search, candidates, partial=False):
    """(Keys holding every search word, best first; up to five that hold the most words) from candidates given as
    (key, id and name texts, tag texts), most popular first. A word matches whole tokens only ("bone" is not in
    herringbone_parquet): 2 points in the id or name, 1 in tags; ties keep the popularity order. With partial, keys
    holding the most words (at least half) count as the matches when none holds every word."""
    words = set(tokens(search))
    scored = []
    for key, names, tags in candidates:
        named, tagged = set(tokens(*names)), set(tokens(*tags))
        found = [word for word in words if word in named or word in tagged]
        scored.append((len(found), sum(2 if word in named else 1 for word in found), key))
    best = sorted((entry for entry in scored if entry[0]), key=lambda entry: (-entry[0], -entry[1]))
    full = [key for count, _score, key in best if count == len(words)]
    if partial and not full and best and 2 * best[0][0] >= len(words):
        full = [key for count, _score, key in best if count == best[0][0]]
    return full, [] if full else [key for _count, _score, key in best[:5]]


def tokens(*texts):
    """Lower-case words of ids, names and tags, split at _ - spaces, camelCase and digits, a plural s dropped."""
    words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+|[0-9]+", re.sub(r"([a-z])([A-Z])", r"\1 \2", " ".join(texts)).lower())
    return [word[:-1] if len(word) > 3 and word.endswith("s") and not word.endswith("ss") else word for word in words]


def poly_haven_maps(files, kind, resolution):
    """{role: {url, md5}} for a resolution of a Poly Haven /files listing (jpg maps, the height as a 16-bit png;
    an HDRI's .hdr)."""
    if kind == "hdri":
        entry = files["hdri"][resolution]
        return {"hdri": entry.get("hdr") or entry["exr"]}
    keys = {**POLY_HAVEN_MAPS, "color": color_key(files)}
    picked = {}
    for role, key in keys.items():
        formats = files.get(key, {}).get(resolution, {})
        # An 8-bit height steps in bump and displacement; the png is 16-bit and lossless (the exr is lossy DWAA).
        order = ("png", "exr", "jpg") if role == "displacement" else ("jpg", "png")
        entry = next((formats[extension] for extension in order if extension in formats), None)
        if entry:
            picked[role] = entry
    if "color" not in picked:
        raise FetchError(f"no colour map at {resolution} among {', '.join(sorted(files))}")
    return picked


def color_key(files):
    """Diffuse, else the first colour variant (col_1, coll1...) of a texture without one."""
    if "Diffuse" in files:
        return "Diffuse"
    return next((key for key in sorted(files) if key.lower().startswith("col")), "Diffuse")


def find_ambientcg(args, closest=None, partial=False):
    include = "include=type,title,tags,dimensions,maps,downloads"
    query = (f"q={urllib.parse.quote_plus(args.search)}&type=material&sort=popular&limit=20" if args.search
             else f"id={urllib.parse.quote(args.asset)}")
    found = get_json(f"{AMBIENTCG}?{query}&{include}")["assets"]
    if args.search and found:
        # ambientCG's own search also matches parts of words and single tags; re-rank like Poly Haven.
        by_id = {asset["id"]: asset for asset in found}
        ranked, near = rank(args.search, [(asset["id"], [asset["id"], asset.get("title", "")], asset.get("tags", []))
                                          for asset in found], partial)
        closest += [f"{other} ({by_id[other].get('title', '')}, ambientcg)" for other in near]
        found = [by_id[asset_id] for asset_id in ranked]
    if not found:
        return None
    asset = found[0]
    if asset.get("type") != "material":
        raise FetchError(f"ambientCG's {asset['id']!r} is a {asset.get('type')}, not a material")
    zips = {item["attributes"]: item for item in asset.get("downloads", []) if item.get("extension") == "zip"}
    resolution = pick_resolution([name.split("-")[0].lower() for name in zips if name.endswith("-JPG")]
                                 or [name.split("-")[0].lower() for name in zips], args.resolution)
    archive = zips.get(f"{resolution.upper()}-JPG") or zips.get(f"{resolution.upper()}-PNG")
    if archive is None:
        raise FetchError(f"ambientCG's {asset['id']!r} offers no zip download ({', '.join(zips) or 'none'})")
    return {
        "source": "ambientcg", "id": asset["id"], "kind": "material", "title": asset.get("title", asset["id"]),
        "authors": [], "page": f"https://ambientcg.com/view?id={asset['id']}", "resolution": resolution,
        "archive": archive["url"], "tags": asset.get("tags", []), "alternatives": [f"{other['id']} ({other.get('title', '')})" for other in found[1:6]],
        **tile(args, (asset.get("dimensions") or {}).get("width", 0) / 100, "material"),  # centimetres
    }


def pick_resolution(available, wanted):
    """The wanted resolution ("2k") if offered, else the largest below it, else the smallest above it."""
    sizes = sorted({int(size.rstrip("kK")) for size in available if size.rstrip("kK").isdigit()})
    if not sizes:
        raise FetchError("the asset lists no downloadable resolutions")
    target = int(wanted.rstrip("k"))
    below = [size for size in sizes if size <= target]
    return f"{below[-1] if below else sizes[0]}k"


def tile(args, width, kind):
    """The tile size in metres: --tile-size, else the scan's real width, else 1 m with a warning."""
    if kind == "hdri" or args.tile_size:
        return {"tileSize": args.tile_size}
    if width > 0:
        return {"tileSize": round(width, 4)}
    return {"tileSize": 1.0, "warnings": ["The scan states no real size; one tile covers 1 m. Set --tile-size to its size."]}


_JSON = {}  # url -> parsed reply, so several assets in one call read each listing once


def get_json(url, missing_ok=False):
    if url in _JSON:
        return _JSON[url]
    try:
        with fetch.open_url(url) as response:
            _JSON[url] = json.load(response)
            return _JSON[url]
    except FetchError as error:
        if missing_ok and str(error).startswith("HTTP 404"):
            return None
        raise
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        raise FetchError(f"{url} returned unreadable JSON ({error})") from None


# --- Downloading -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def download_poly_haven(asset, folder, max_bytes):
    files = {}
    for role, entry in asset["files"].items():
        name = fetch.file_name_from_url(entry["url"])
        path = os.path.join(folder, name)
        if not (os.path.isfile(path) and md5(path) == entry.get("md5")):
            fetch.http_get(entry["url"], path, max_bytes)
        files[role] = name
    return files


def download_ambientcg(asset, folder, max_bytes):
    """Download the zip and keep only its map images (it also holds a .blend, .usdc and .mtlx, which stay unread)."""
    archive = os.path.join(folder, f"{asset['id']}_{asset['resolution']}.zip")
    fetch.http_get(asset["archive"], archive, max_bytes)
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as bundle:
            members = ambientcg_maps(bundle.namelist())
            if "color" not in members:
                raise FetchError(f"ambientCG's {asset['id']} zip has no colour map; it holds {', '.join(bundle.namelist())}")
            files = {role: os.path.basename(member) for role, member in members.items()}
            for role, member in members.items():
                with bundle.open(member) as source, open(os.path.join(folder, files[role]), "wb") as target:
                    target.write(source.read())
    except zipfile.BadZipFile:
        raise FetchError(f"ambientCG's download for {asset['id']} is not a valid zip") from None
    finally:
        os.remove(archive)
    return files


def ambientcg_maps(names):
    """{role: zip member} from ambientCG's <Id>_<Res>-<FMT>_<Map>.<ext> member names."""
    found = {}
    for name in names:
        stem, extension = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(name))
        for role, suffix in AMBIENTCG_MAPS.items():
            if extension.lower() in (".jpg", ".png") and stem.endswith("_" + suffix):
                found[role] = name
    return found


def md5(path):
    digest = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def next_command(args, record):
    """The Blender command that reuses this download: the same options, naming the asset that was found."""
    dropped, carried, skip = {"--download-only": 0, "--search": 1, "--asset": 1, "--source": 1}, [], 0
    for token in fetch.script_args():
        flag = token.split("=", 1)[0]
        if skip or flag in dropped:
            skip = skip - 1 if skip else (0 if "=" in token else dropped[flag])
            continue
        carried.append(token)
    command = ["blender", "-b", "--factory-startup", "--python", os.path.abspath(__file__), "--",
               "--asset", record["id"], "--source", record["source"]]
    # --project alone downloads before a scene exists; the Blender step still needs the scene to wire.
    return " ".join(shlex.quote(part) for part in command + carried) + ("" if args.blend else " --blend <scene.blend>")


def batch_next_command(args, jobs):
    """The one Blender command that reuses a batch's downloads, naming each asset that was found."""
    dropped, carried, skip = {"--download-only": 0, "--world": 1, "--material": 1, "--search": 1, "--asset": 1}, [], 0
    for token in fetch.script_args():
        flag = token.split("=", 1)[0]
        if skip or flag in dropped:
            skip = skip - 1 if skip else (0 if "=" in token else dropped[flag])
            continue
        carried.append(token)
    found = [part for job in jobs for part in (["--asset", job.found] if not hasattr(job, "fallback_search") else
                                               ["--world", job.found] if job.hdri else
                                               ["--material", f"{job.objects}={job.found}"])]
    command = ["blender", "-b", "--factory-startup", "--python", os.path.abspath(__file__), "--", *found]
    return " ".join(shlex.quote(part) for part in command + carried) + ("" if args.blend else " --blend <scene.blend>")


# --- Wiring it in Blender ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def apply(args, record):
    import bpy

    if not args.blend or not os.path.isfile(args.blend):
        raise FetchError(f"no .blend at {args.blend}; save the scene first and pass it to --blend")
    blend = os.path.abspath(args.blend)
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=blend)
    # --tile-size also overrides the size recorded by an earlier download of the same asset.
    record = {**record, "tileSize": args.tile_size or record["tileSize"]}
    paths = {role: os.path.join(record["folder"], name) for role, name in record["files"].items()}
    warnings = list(record.get("warnings", []))
    report = {"kind": record["kind"], "asset": record["id"], "title": record["title"], "blend": blend,
              "files": paths, "credit": record["credit"], "license": record["license"],
              "attribution": record["attribution"], "alternatives": record.get("alternatives", [])}
    if record["kind"] == "hdri":
        report["world"] = shading.build_world(bpy, paths["hdri"], args.strength, args.rotation)
    else:
        objects = named_objects(bpy, args.objects)
        pattern = regular_pattern(record) if args.anti_tiling == "auto" else None
        if pattern:
            warnings.append(f"Anti-tiling is off for a regular pattern ({pattern}): a shifted copy would show ghost "
                            "joints. Pass --anti-tiling on to force it.")
        anti_tiling = args.anti_tiling == "on" or (args.anti_tiling == "auto" and not pattern)
        material, scale = shading.build_material(bpy, record, paths, objects, args, anti_tiling, warnings)
        for obj in objects:
            assign(obj, material)
        report.update(material=material.name, objects=[obj.name for obj in objects], mapping=args.mapping,
                      tileSize=record["tileSize"] if args.mapping == "box" else None, mappingScale=scale,
                      antiTiling=anti_tiling, variation=args.variation)
        if not objects:
            warnings.append(f"No --objects: material {material.name!r} is in the file but on nothing.")
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend)
    report["warnings"] = warnings
    return report


def regular_pattern(record):
    """The word in the scan's id, title or tags that marks a laid pattern (bricks, tiles, planks), else None."""
    words = set(tokens(record["id"], record.get("title", "")))
    # Tags and categories also name uses ("floor", "panel", "deck"); trust only unambiguous words there. Ids and
    # titles still miss some: Poly Haven's marble_01 is tiles only by its tags.
    tagged = set(tokens(*record.get("tags", []))) & TAG_PATTERNS
    found = sorted((words & REGULAR_PATTERNS) | tagged) or (["wood floor"] if {"wood", "floor"} <= words else [])
    return found[0] if found else None


def named_objects(bpy, names):
    wanted = [name.strip() for name in names.split(",") if name.strip()]
    missing = [name for name in wanted if name not in bpy.data.objects]
    if missing:
        meshes = sorted(obj.name for obj in bpy.data.objects if obj.type == "MESH")
        raise FetchError(f"no object named {', '.join(missing)}; meshes: {', '.join(meshes[:40]) or 'none'}")
    objects = [bpy.data.objects[name] for name in wanted]
    unusable = [obj.name for obj in objects if not hasattr(obj.data, "materials")]
    if unusable:
        raise FetchError(f"{', '.join(unusable)} cannot hold a material")
    return objects


def assign(obj, material):
    """Every material slot gets the material; an object without slots gets one."""
    if not obj.material_slots:
        obj.data.materials.append(material)
    for slot in obj.material_slots:
        slot.material = material


if __name__ == "__main__":
    code = main()
    sys.stdout.flush()
    sys.stderr.flush()
    if code:
        # Blender keeps running (and exits 0) after a --python script returns; leave with the code.
        os._exit(code)

"""Look kit CLI: one command gives an arbitrary scene a finished look (lighting, atmosphere, weather, lens).

    blender -b scene.blend --python look.py -- --look rain-night [--quality preview|final] [--set key=val ...]
        [--save [OUT.blend]] [--render OUT.png [--frame N]] [--animation OUT_DIR/ [--budget-min 15]] [--percent P]
    blender -b scene.blend --python look.py -- --remove [--save]
    blender -b --python look.py -- --list            (looks, layers, every parameter with its default)

Looks: rain-night, fog-forest, neon-interior, night-city, golden-hour, overcast, studio-product, wet-product.
Layers (alone, on top of the scene's own lighting): fog, godrays, rain, snow, wet, practicals, camera.

What it does: reads the scene (camera, subject in frame, ground, emissive objects, indoor/outdoor), then adds
tagged objects only (custom property ``look_kit``): world sky, a sun, practical lights at every emissive object,
a height-fog volume, a hidden light blocker for shafts, rain/snow geometry nodes with splashes, a removable wet
node in each material, water beads, a softbox rig. Sets EEVEE (ray tracing, volumetrics, shadows) or Cycles
for --quality final where the look needs it, AgX + contrast look, auto exposure from a small probe render,
bloom, depth of field, lens distortion, vignette and grain. Re-running replaces the previous look; --remove
undoes it. The user's objects are never deleted (their sun lamps are hidden by night/studio looks).

Prints one line ``LOOK_JSON {...}`` (what it did, timings, files) on stdout; exits 1 with ``look: error: ...``.
`--save` with no path overwrites the opened .blend. Also importable: ``import look; look.apply(scene, name)``.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class LookError(Exception):
    pass


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise LookError(message)


def parse(argv):
    p = Parser(prog="look.py", allow_abbrev=False, description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--look", help="look or layer name")
    p.add_argument("--quality", default="preview", choices=["preview", "final"])
    p.add_argument("--set", action="append", default=[], metavar="KEY=VAL", help="override a parameter (see --list)")
    p.add_argument("--save", nargs="?", const="", default=None, metavar="OUT.blend")
    p.add_argument("--render", metavar="OUT.png", help="render one still after applying")
    p.add_argument("--frame", type=int, help="frame for --render (default: the scene's current frame)")
    p.add_argument("--animation", metavar="OUT_DIR",
                   help="render the scene's frame range with blender's render-final.py into OUT_DIR (final.mp4, preview.mp4 early)")
    p.add_argument("--budget-min", type=float, default=15,
                   help="--animation: wall-clock minutes; it fits samples/size/engine and returns before this (default 15)")
    p.add_argument("--percent", type=int, help="render size as a percentage of the scene's resolution")
    p.add_argument("--remove", action="store_true", help="undo the look kit")
    p.add_argument("--list", action="store_true")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    if not (a.list or a.remove or a.look):
        raise LookError("give --look NAME, --remove or --list")
    return a


def main(argv):
    try:
        a = parse(argv)
        import bpy
        import look
        if a.list:
            print("LOOK_JSON " + json.dumps(look.list_looks()))
            return 0
        scene = bpy.context.scene
        out = {}
        t0 = time.time()
        if a.remove:
            look.remove(scene)
            out["removed"] = True
        else:
            overrides = {}
            for kv in a.set:
                if "=" not in kv:
                    raise LookError(f"--set wants KEY=VAL, got {kv!r}")
                k, v = kv.split("=", 1)
                overrides[k.strip()] = v.strip()
            if a.percent:
                scene.render.resolution_percentage = a.percent
            if a.frame is not None:
                scene.frame_set(a.frame)
            try:
                out = look.apply(scene, a.look, quality=a.quality, **overrides)
            except ValueError as e:
                raise LookError(str(e))
        files = []
        if a.save is not None:
            path = a.save or bpy.data.filepath
            if not path:
                raise LookError("--save needs a path (the scene was never saved)")
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), exist_ok=True)
            bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=os.path.abspath(path), copy=bool(a.save) and a.save != bpy.data.filepath)
            files.append(os.path.abspath(path))
        if a.render:
            r = scene.render
            r.filepath = os.path.abspath(a.render)
            r.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
            t = time.time()
            look.render.safe_render(scene, write_still=True)
            out["render_s"] = round(time.time() - t, 2)
            files.append(r.filepath)
        if a.animation:
            # The budgeted final renderer lives beside this script; it always returns a video
            # inside --budget-min.
            import subprocess
            render_final = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "render-final.py")
            if not os.path.isfile(render_final):
                raise LookError(f"--animation needs the blender skill's render-final.py at {os.path.normpath(render_final)}")
            folder = os.path.abspath(a.animation)
            os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
            blend = os.path.abspath(a.save) if a.save else os.path.join(folder, "scene.blend")
            if not a.save:
                bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend, copy=True)
            # Run render-final in Blender's own Python: no system python3 is needed (macOS sys.executable is Blender).
            t = time.time()
            result = subprocess.run(
                [bpy.app.binary_path, "-b", "--factory-startup", "--python-exit-code", "1", "--python", render_final,
                 "--", blend, "--out", folder, "--budget-min", str(a.budget_min), "--blender", bpy.app.binary_path],
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
            if result.returncode:
                raise LookError(f"render-final.py failed ({result.returncode}); see its message above")
            summary = [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("{")]
            if not summary:
                raise LookError("render-final.py printed no summary; see its message above")
            out["animation"] = json.loads(summary[-1])
            out["animation_s"] = round(time.time() - t, 2)
            files.append(out["animation"].get("video", folder))
        if look.render.FALLBACK:
            out.update(look.render.FALLBACK)
            out["gpu"] = False
        out["files"] = files
        out["total_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        print("LOOK_JSON " + json.dumps(out), flush=True)
        return 0
    except LookError as e:
        print(f"look: error: {e}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        return 1
    except Exception as e:  # report Blender/API failures in one line, not a traceback wall
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        print(f"look: error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    code = main(argv)
    if code:
        sys.exit(code)
